notes.title: We Need Your Nomination + Autumn Sale!
notes.content:
Calling all players! The 2023 Steam Awards have begun, and it would mean the *world* to myself and our whole team if you would [b]nominate 8-Bit Adventures 2 for the Outstanding Story-Rich Game award by clicking the link below[/b] 😊

[b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/733110/view/3782520875866065175]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/733110/view/3782520875866065175[/url][/b]

And if you've never played 8-Bit Adventures 2 before, now's a great time to jump in! As part of the Steam Autumn Sale, the game [b]is 30% Off - our BIGGEST discount ever[/b]! 🥳

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

8-Bit Adventures 1 is also 60% Off too!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/370300/8Bit_Adventures_1_The_Forgotten_Journey_Remastered_Edition/

The Steam Awards began in 2016, one year after 8-Bit Adventures 1 came out. And then 8-Bit Adventures 2 was in development for 7 years. So this year marks the first time that a big game I've developed has ever been eligible to participate in the Awards! And [b]we only get one chance[/b] (because 2023 is our year of release).

As many of you know, it's been incredibly difficult to draw attention to 8-Bit Adventures 2. I've tried everything I can think of, but one of the most common comments I receive from new players is still "Why haven't I heard of this game before?"

[b]The Steam Awards are, quite genuinely, a life-changing opportunity for us[/b] to bring 8-Bit Adventures 2 to a mainstream audience. [b]If you've enjoyed the game and want to support our future endeavors,[/b] I would be *immensely* grateful for your support in nominating 8-Bit Adventures 2 for the Outstanding Story-Rich Game award.
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/733110/view/3782520875866065175]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/6240fdf937c2c5ae4e1b866e7159a06f68562dea.png[/img][/url]

Sebastian, Jerram, Sufyan, and I poured everything we had into making this game, so seeing players enjoy it and connect with the story has been one of the most satisfying experiences of my life. I'm immensely proud of our Very Positive rating on Steam - which is entirely thanks to players like you.

If you're wondering why we're targeting the Outstanding Story-Rich Game category, [b]Steam only allows us to select one award to be nominated for.[/b] While several other options were considered, 8-Bit Adventures 2 is - ultimately - a story-focused game, in a story-focused genre. And based on comments from players, [b]it's a story that's really connected with people[/b] - which I couldn't be happier about.

But don't take my word for it. I want to share some public-facing [b]quotes from players about why our game is Story-Rich - and why 8-Bit Adventures 2 is worthy of your nomination[/b] 😊

This is only a very small selection of spoiler-free comments I've received from players. Thank you SO much to everyone who's taken the time to share their thoughts on the game. It makes my day every time I read one, and it's sincerely a big help!

So if you think we deserve it, [b]please take a moment to nominate 8-Bit Adventures 2 by following the link below[/b]  👇

I'll be doing a proper update post in December, as well as releasing a new game update with bug fixes, a restored April Fools' boss, and something fun for the Holiday Season. And the game's Free DLC is progressing very well! [b]But for now, please show us your support - and let's make 8-Bit Adventures 2 a success together![/b] 🥰

notes.title: Summer Sale Deals + News & Future Teases!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! It's been a little while, but I'm back with a new update to celebrate the Steam Summer Sale! We'll cover the latest deals, some fresh news, and a tiny tease of the future...

But first, I'm excited to announce that 8-Bit Adventures 2 has now sold over 3000 copies! 🥳 It's a solid start, and what's most exciting is that more than a third of those copies were sold *after* the game's launch month.

To me, this shows that 8-Bit Adventures 2 is a game with legs - and that's absolutely thanks to the great word of mouth and positive Steam reviews from players. Thank you all so much for that - your passion and support mean the world to me 🥰

Our next goal is to reach 500 Steam Reviews and receive an Overwhelmingly Positive rating - that way, we'll get more attention from Steam's algorithms. We're already at 114 reviews, so if you enjoyed the game and want to support us, please consider leaving one of your own! 😊

Now, onto the Discounts! (News and Teases are further below)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/e55df4a353c80f95091c28e7e9d33a5d8f760c79.png[/img]

[h2]8-Bit Adventures 2[/h2]
From now until July 13th at 10am PDT, you can get 8-Bit Adventures 2 for 20% Off ($15.99 USD)!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

You can also get the incredible Soundtrack for 20% Off ($7.99 USD), or the Game + Soundtrack Bundle for just $23.99 USD!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2281060/8Bit_Adventures_2_Soundtrack/

[h2]8-Bit Adventures 1[/h2]
While you can jump into 8-Bit Adventures 2 without any prior experience, I've learnt that a lot of players really want to get the full story. 

So for the next twelve days, you can also get 8-Bit Adventures 1 for 60% Off ($3.99 USD)!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/370300/8Bit_Adventures_1_The_Forgotten_Journey_Remastered_Edition/

The first game's wonderful Soundtrack is 30% Off ($3.49 USD), or you can get the 8-Bit Adventures 1 Game + Soundtrack Bundle for only $6.59 USD! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/387170/8Bit_Adventures__Soundtrack__Composers_Selection/

[h2]Tales Across Time[/h2]
Finally, you can also get our experimental, short-story RPG Tales Across Time for just $2.39 USD! This game was like a testing ground for ideas I was considering for 8-Bit Adventures 2 after finishing 8BA1. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/461710/Tales_Across_Time/

[h2]Behind-the-Scenes News and Updates[/h2]
So what's been going on since we last caught up? Well, there's been great progress with the 8-Bit Adventures 2 console ports going on at Ratalaika Games. In fact, I'll be receiving a new test build in the coming week - which I'm very excited about! 😁 

Because I'm not handling the porting process myself, there's not much that I can share beyond that; but there has been a LOT of progress (in the past month especially), so the project is definitely on-track!

[h2]Free DLC[/h2]
What I *have* been working on myself is the upcoming Free DLC for 8-Bit Adventures 2! The sprawling dungeon that this content takes place in has now been completed. It's over 50 Maps in size - divided into 9 Areas across 3 Tiers - and every area is different. 

The format of the dungeon is much more open and free-flowing than normal, so I'm excited to see what players think! It even has a town inside it - which you can see just a little of below. It has ties to a location in the main game, so I'm curious to see if anyone recognises it 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/416bdeec374966fb173bc28c9043dcda57aed93c.png[/img]
Sebastian has also been hard at work on some music for the Free DLC, and just recently completed a new boss battle theme which I think chiptune fans are going to really enjoy!

Truth be told, after seven years of development on 8BA2, I've been feeling pretty burnt-out since the Steam release (as well as all the post-launch bug fixing that we did). And this Free DLC ended up being much more ambitious than I originally intended - so I apologise for the wait! But I want to make it as special as I can, as thanks to everyone who's enjoyed the game 😊

Next up I'm working on the boss battles, and then I'll be implementing the story content (which currently exists in Word document form haha). 8BA2's long development taught me the dangers of showing off content too early, so please stay tuned for a proper showcase later this year! But here's a little silhouette tease of the two totally new bosses in the Free DLC 😁

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/d9c658e09f07b3614c42b901f9f39dd8b0710784.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/1e75a09271bb87c3faf90b46b106e811e07670c5.png[/img]
[h2]Future Project[/h2]
Finally, I've also been working on the game design plans for our next project, which two incredible artists have already begun preparing assets for as well! The idea is that we prepare as much as can in pre-production, so that once I'm ready to begin active development, we already have a lot of what we need ready to go 🥳 

I won't be able to announce what this project is for a while yet, but the goal is to have a short turn-around on this one (around a year and a half of development), so you probably won't have to wait *too* long 😉

In general, I want to start designing and developing projects which can be released in a much more reasonable space of time (e.g. less than 3 years, as opposed to 8BA2's 7+ years). 

That will require a smaller scope than 8-Bit Adventures 2 (at least, in some respects), but my hope is that with a more focused game we can continue to push the production values higher. Don't worry about a lesser or altered experience though - I definitely want to keep making more story-driven, Japanese-style RPGs with turn-based combat and a World Map! I just want to find a way to do it that provides more regular content for players, and doesn't totally consume my life haha. 

All of this will depend on my finances - as most things sadly do - but I'll do my best! 😁
~Josh

notes.title: Steam Deck Verified, Text Speed Options, Bug Fixes, Guides, & Interviews!
notes.content:
[h3]It's been one month since 8-Bit Adventures 2 launched on Steam & GOG  🥳 [/h3]

Honestly, writing that feels a little surreal! Thank you so, so much to everyone who has supported the game in that time 🥰

While we're still working towards financial sustainability, the response from players and reviewers has been [b]incredible[/b]. We've had 77 reviews from players on Steam so far, [b]and achieved a Very Positive rating![/b] This has really helped us a lot; I noticed that Steam started sharing the game a lot more when we initially hit Positive, and then again at Very Positive. So a massive thanks to everyone who's taken the time to share their thoughts! They've been a genuine joy to read 😊

And now, thanks to a new review from [url=https://www.rpgfan.com/review/8-bit-adventures-2/]RPGFan[/url] (check it out by clicking on the link), we've also achieved an OpenCritic Rating of Mighty (the highest a game can receive), placing us near the top of their [url=https://opencritic.com/browse/all/2023/score]Best Video Games of 2023 list[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/2336c9b9f0989aaf1ff0b4b59dde22354a5e3a1f.png[/img]

And that's not all! We've also received a Metacritic Score of 87, which should appear on the Steam page soon too 🥳

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/24c1375e8a674ea13d22b1f255a6cd4a65af72e3.png[/img]

But most of all, I've been especially grateful for the people who have reached out and told me how much they've enjoyed the game - whether for its story, its characters, its music, its visuals, its combat, its sense of exploration, etc. It's been incredibly humbling and gratifying, and so I just wanted to express my gratitude. The community around 8-Bit Adventures 2 has been absolutely wonderful to interact with, and that's thanks to all of you 😊

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

[h2]Steam Deck Verified![/h2]
I'm thrilled to say that, as of February 9th, 8-Bit Adventures 2 has been classified as Steam Deck Verified by Valve! It was totally out-of-the-blue, but since so many players were asking about Deck compatibility, I'm really glad that it happened so soon after launch. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/00bf2737f05b3e9d60c4541b0b0adb63381d013a.png[/img]

I've also now had many reports from players that the game is working really well on the Steam Deck! So if that's your preferred platform, 8-Bit Adventures 2 is ready and waiting for you 🥳

[h2]Text Speed Options[/h2]

One of the most requested additions to 8-Bit Adventures 2 since its release was more text speed options. And I'm happy to say that these were included in the February 16th Update!

While the way the game is set-up made large changes difficult, we were able to take feedback on-board and incorporate some new features. 

First off, you no longer need to hold the Confirm button to speed up the text; one simple press will speed it up now. Additionally, the speed up function will now cut off at the end of the current text box, preventing you from accidentally skipping through multiple boxes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/4a68ca31dd31d74b4e019fad07424fa27bb80fbf.png[/img]

Finally, a new Option has been added, allowing the player to choose between Normal text speed and Fast text speed. Essentially, the Fast text speed makes our current optional speed-up function automatic and always on. I still recommend Normal text speed, as this is timed with the choreography of cutscenes, and provides a stronger narrative experience in my view. But for anyone who wanted faster text, I hope these options address your concerns!

Please note that, while the speed-up function has been thoroughly tested, the Fast text speed system may have some unforeseen issues in certain cutscenes. They should only be minor issues at most, but if you run into any, please do let me know!

[h2]Community Guides[/h2]

I wanted to take a moment to shout-out two members of the community who created some excellent guides for players. Note that both guides contain spoilers!

The first is the Court Room Guide by the awesome dragon_blade. This guide will help you to achieve a "Not Guilty!" verdict, and gain the best possible rewards.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2928255212
And the second is "Augments and You, a Party Build guide" by the wonderful SupahVi! She'll teach you one way to build a super-powered RPG party in 8-Bit Adventures 2, including Augments to Equip and character combinations to use. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2929560492
Thanks to dragon_blade and SupahVi for creating these for the community! 😊

[h2]Bug Fixes and Updates[/h2]

Over the past month, Sufyan (our programmer) and I have fixed dozens of bugs reported to us by the community. Thank you very much for all of your feedback; it's been a big help. In fact, as of this past weekend, we've finally exhausted the list of reported bugs! So the game should be incredibly solid at this point (famous last words 😋).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/e57d6752c393fe9cda5b3ef570c15821953253a1.png[/img]

This included everything from the addition of an ultimate Axe weapon that had been accidentally left out of the game, to balance changes and bug fixes (including one fight that became unwinnable if you followed a particular order of actions), to an additional shop added before a boss fight, to an overhaul of the turn-speed calculations to make sure that every build was viable and enemies weren't getting an unfair number of turns.

If you want to see what's changed, please check out the patch notes on the 8-Bit Adventures 2 Steam Community!

[h2]Interviews[/h2]

Finally, I wanted to share a couple of new interviews with everyone!

First off, we have an interview that our composer Sebastian Cruz did with the DeltronZ Youtube Channel, all about composing for 8-Bit Adventures 2: 

[previewyoutube=LGIWAadpnNQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Del has been a massive supporter of the game. He interviewed me in late January, and has actually been doing a full playthrough of 8-Bit Adventures 2, which is really enjoyable! But the interview with Sebastian is really good, and I highly recommend it - even I learnt some new things! 🥰

And then we also have another new interview that I recorded LIVE with NinjaGuyX and Gladiator50n on Youtube:

[previewyoutube=1ABmTIlOw9w;full][/previewyoutube]
It was a ton of fun, and I think we talked about some interesting topics (including the future), so I hope that anyone interested might enjoy checking it out.

Finally, there's a written interview I did with Kosuke Seki from a media outlet in Japan called Game*Spark! It's entirely in Japanese, but for any fluent speakers, I thought you might find it interesting: https://www.gamespark.jp/article/2023/02/28/127507.html

A big thanks to Del, NinjaGuyX, Gladiator50n, and Kosuke for getting in touch and making these happen. I really appreciate the support 😊
[hr][/hr]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f07395216d5a455821c9c0b2f76e8f06c876ec35.png[/img]

Thanks so much for reading this update everyone! As always, if you have any questions or comments, please feel free to share them on the Steam forum, on Twitter, via my email (josh@criticalgames.com.au), or by joining up to our Discord linked below (which has a great RPG-loving community)! 

Finally, I mentioned last time that there's a hint towards the Free DLC in the game already, but I've only seen a couple of people mention it so far 😉
~Josh

notes.title: Thank You, Free DLC Tease, Steam Deck, & Trading Cards!
notes.content:
[h3]It's been a big week.[/h3]

8-Bit Adventures 2 is finally out on Steam & GOG, and we've had an incredible outpouring of support from so many. I've been genuinely touched by the number of kind, considerate, and uplifting messages folks have sent me, and reading them has absolutely made the last 7 years of work feel worthwhile. 

[i]Especially[/i] since my dear grandmother has had to go into a nursing home this past week, due to Alzheimer's, and that's taken a big emotional toll on my family and I (along with all the work involved). She was always one of my biggest supporters, and it's been a little sad to have finally reached the release of 8-Bit Adventures 2, but with her now unable to understand what I've done. 

So with that going on in the background, receiving your messages has been especially meaningful for me, and it's made me feel very appreciative of our community. From the bottom of my heart, thank you for all of your kindness and support - it genuinely means the world to me.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

[b]I'm also thrilled to say that we've had over 1000 sales, and have nearly recouped the cost of the game's development![/b] We've even made it onto the top of the JRPG New and Trending list this week 😊 That's a wonderful start and I'm immensely grateful to everyone who's bought a copy of 8-Bit Adventures 2. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/726943cfd7794b4f5dabd9c6131b042d25428ada.png[/img]

We've still got a long way to go to make the game a success and earn enough money to fund future projects, but I'm confident that we'll get there in the long-run. I've already seen lots of people sharing the word with friends and followers, and that sincerely means a lot! Word of mouth is an indie developer's biggest support 😁

The only other thing I'd ask is that if you're enjoying the game, then please consider leaving us a review. If we can get to 50 positive reviews, we'll earn the Very Positive status - and that's a big help on Steam!

Anyway, with all that out of the way, I wanted to talk about what's going on at the moment, and tease the future of 8-Bit Adventures 2! [b](The Free DLC Tease is further below)[/b] [hr][/hr]
[h2]Updates and Fixes[/h2]
Unfortunately like any game launch, there have been some bugs which snuck through our rigorous testing. I'm sincerely sorry for these issues, and for any impact they may have on your experience with 8-Bit Adventures 2. 

I've updated the game every day since launch, and am trying to respond to issues as quickly as possible. The same goes for our fantastic programmer Sufyan, who's worked to fix some of the particularly nasty issues! Please check the Patch Notes for a rundown of what's been fixed so far.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/88ca065f919d05d29464c6c6c55f6b51fda0f480.gif[/img]
[i]Pictured above is the good ol' humping glitch. This was fixed years ago, but is still one of the funniest bugs we encountered![/i]

If a problem arises, we'll do whatever we can to fix it. So please let us know if you run into any issues via the Steam forums, Twitter, or our Discord (linked at the bottom of this post). 
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Soundtrack Available Everywhere![/h2]
While I'm sure everyone knows that you can purchase the 8-Bit Adventures 2 Soundtrack on Steam, you may not have realised that you can also listen to the Soundtrack on Spotify, Youtube Music, iTunes, Deezer, Pandora, Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, iHeartRadio, and more! 

[url=https://open.spotify.com/album/3nTKB7c1fdr07XjgGEFk2q][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/e36b41b41c3ee851e1946d29b96156038aa40053.png[/img][/url]

The Soundtrack includes 78 songs pulled from the game, plus 7 dramatic orchestral arrangements - all composed by the wonderful Sebastian "Carfonu" Cruz! 

So wherever you listen to music, please check it out and show him some love 😊
[hr][/hr]
[h2]More Reviews![/h2]
Since my last post, there have been even more reviews for 8-Bit Adventures 2. If anyone's still on the fence, please check them out, as I think they're all [b]very[/b] well-written & interesting looks at the game. [list]
[*] [b]RPGLMNTZ Review[/b] - [url=https://rpglmntz.com/2023/01/31/8-bit-adventures-2-rpg-review/]https://rpglmntz.com/2023/01/31/8-bit-adventures-2-rpg-review/[/url]

[*] [b]Turn-Based Lovers Review[/b] - [url=https://turnbasedlovers.com/review/8-bit-adventures-2-brings-back-the-classics-impressions/?amp=1]https://turnbasedlovers.com/review/8-bit-adventures-2-brings-back-the-classics-impressions/?amp=1[/url]

[*] [b]Chalgyr's Game Room Review[/b] - [url=https://www.chalgyr.com/2023/02/8bit-adventures-2-pc-review.html]https://www.chalgyr.com/2023/02/8bit-adventures-2-pc-review.html[/url]

[*] [b]Tech-Gaming Review[/b] - [url=https://www.tech-gaming.com/8-bit-adventures-2/]https://www.tech-gaming.com/8-bit-adventures-2/[/url][/list] [hr][/hr]
[h2]Steam Deck[/h2]
Since I've had a lot of people ask me about Steam Deck, I just wanted to explain the situation.

Essentially, Valve wouldn't give me access to the Steam Deck tools, or consider approving the game for Steam Deck. And since I live in Australia, I can't buy a Deck to test the game on myself. As such, I relied on the testimonies of a couple of reviewers, who both very kindly gave me feedback on the performance and informed me that the game has issues like lag, frame drops, and long loads.

But now that it's out, I'm hearing reports from players that the game is actually running quite well. We have fixed a couple of memory leaks around launch, so that could be helping with the Deck performance as well. 

So if you'd like to play on Steam Deck, my recommendation is to try the free demo, and see how it performs for you. Hopefully I'll be able to get an official stamp of approval from Valve sometime in the future! 
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Trading Cards and Community Items[/h2]
Valve requires that newly released games reach a certain number of players and be out for a certain number of days before Trading Cards and Community Items can be implemented.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/9a61988b22f3b763e8c68b55222177613bb030b8.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/a1d0058be36feaf871bda41b25624506c6e5c7f7.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/d1563e4835ae0f970bf2614b11fb513ac0bb80bd.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/5f0e2354c0b45d1c91f199ac6106fe64eb4f1d75.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f0c1da018f6c064c16cea87b233cc156dc4e821d.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/2bd615087fe09bf4f121555d4dd8d48602efa3ca.png[/img]

I'm happy to say that Valve have just today granted me the ability to send our Trading Cards and Community Items to them for review, so they should hopefully be added to the game this week!
[hr][/hr]
[h2]A New Place to Buy - Itch.io![/h2]
At the suggestion of a good friend, I've now made 8-Bit Adventures 1 and 2 available on Itch.io! So if you prefer that storefront, then please check it out. 

[b]8-Bit Adventures 1:[/b] https://criticalgames.itch.io/8-bit-adventures-1

[b]8-Bit Adventures 2:[/b] https://criticalgames.itch.io/8-bit-adventures-2

[url=https://criticalgames.itch.io/8-bit-adventures-2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/8587c6ce7374ac3d9a98094ddfac3ad3396159d1.png[/img][/url]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]8-Bit Adventures 1 + 2 Bundle[/h2]
Due to requests from players, I'm working on an 8-Bit Adventures 1 + 2 Bundle which will sell for a small discount and include both games.

[b]This bundle is scheduled to launch on Steam and GOG on the 10th of February at 6am PST![/b]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Free DLC is on the way![/h2]
Finally, I wanted to offer a small glimpse at what’s to come. As some of you may know, I’ve been planning and developing some Free Post-Game DLC for 8-Bit Adventures 2.

While I’d wanted to get the Free DLC released only 1-2 months after release, there’s still a lot left to do. And to be completely honest, the last couple of months have been extremely intense, ‘round-the-clock work with constant late nights; so I feel I need to recharge and take it slow for a little while. Seven years is a long time to go without a break 😅

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/faaaef479b02da8b4a54aaa8858baf742b047097.png[/img]

[b]([url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]Check our Twitter[/url] for the animated version - Steam's file size restrictions wouldn't let me upload it)[/b]

The Free DLC begins with you discovering a new location, sequestered deep in the woods. Called the Shrine of Slumber, it will force you to face foes old and new in high level challenges – all while unravelling a story from the ancient past, long lost to [i]conscious[/i] memory.

There might even be a hint to the Free DLC hidden in the game already 😉
[hr][/hr]
Thanks for reading everyone - and for all of your support! I'll have even more news soon, so please keep an eye out for it 😊

For more information and updates, please:

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 Twitter Showcase Round-Up #4 + Mini-Trailer!
notes.content:
Guess what, everyone? [b]We're now just 3 DAYS away from 8-Bit Adventures 2's big launch on PC (Steam & GOG) on January 31st![/b] (With console versions coming later this year) 🥳

If you want to support our work and help us have a successful launch, then please consider wishlisting 8-Bit Adventures 2 here on Steam using the button below. It's been making a massive difference for us behind-the-scenes, and I'm now really hopeful that we can make it to the front page of Steam!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

I'm back again to share a fourth and FINAL round-up of info, screenshots, and music samples from 8-Bit Adventures 2 that I've been posting on social media (this time from January)!

[b]But first, it's time for our final new video - the Airships and World Map Trailer![/b] To no one's surprise, it focuses on exploring our World Map - both on-foot and via your very own Airship!

8-Bit Adventures 2 features a richly detailed World Map, filled with secrets & optional areas to discover! Our world's full of the character-driven Side-Quests and challenging Super Boss battles that RPG fans expect 😊

[previewyoutube=g3paGhsldnk;full][/previewyoutube]
That's the last of the four trailers we've released this month, so I really hope everyone enjoyed them =) If you've missed any of them, please check out my past posts! 

[hr][/hr][h2]Party Swapping[/h2] In 8-Bit Adventures 2, you can swap allies into battle at any time – without even wasting a turn!

Low on HP? Swap! Can't take advantage of enemy weaknesses? Bring in someone who can!

Swapping means you always have access to all 7 party members in battle!⚔️

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/46af0fb2f7e232d1bb081ff9c4165aaef6aca627.gif[/img]

It's hard to show in a single post, but Swapping adds an extra layer of strategy to combat in 8-Bit Adventures 2, and makes late game battles feel very dynamic! Plus everyone in the party always earns full EXP from battle 👍

[hr][/hr][h2]Combo and Trio Abilities[/h2] 8-Bit Adventures 2 lets party members team up & unleash powerful Combo or Trio Abilities!

These include Abilities which both heal & boost Defence, allow single target Magic to hit all enemies, freeze & instantly K.O a foe, or summon a giant Meteor!

There are 11 Combo & Trio Abilities in total, and we tried to make them all unique. Trio Abilities make you feel like you’re really giving everything you’ve got! 💪

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/33783d363ee12796e8a6d1bba6f20e8d33f5d329.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Music Sample #7[/h2] This energetic music sample follows last week's trailer, which showed a war-torn industrial realm called the Processor 🎵

Each area of this dungeon has its own theme. This song accompanies a deadly train ride as you fight your way across the carriage roofs!

[previewyoutube=Ai37DstkmuQ;full][/previewyoutube]
The full 8-Bit Adventures 2 soundtrack features 85 songs and it launches alongside the PC release (Steam & GOG) on January 31st 2023!

[hr][/hr][h2]Cinematic Shots[/h2] The story of 8-Bit Adventures 2 features numerous Cinematic Shots like these - detailed pieces of art which show the world from a new perspective.

Sprinkled throughout the narrative, they ensure that epic moments have a big impact! 🤩

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/00fae3901b1118b448b71151af7bb14f82b3128d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/235141d158ca90dcce7ab87b426a4b9d1e774d6e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/09c82c1d075317223125e82fd119f1c317051542.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/fe7be18d9ae2ed52eea294b7c982c7f21898f888.png[/img]

Our approach to these images was inspired by cutscenes in the NES Ninja Gaiden trilogy, as well as in classic Phantasy Star games 😊

[hr][/hr][h2]Glade of Graphics[/h2] The Glade of Graphics is a hidden valley with Art Deco style. Here, an eccentric group of robot artists endeavor to imitate humanity - in order to perfect their craft.

But a death in the Glade kicks off a murder mystery that no one wants to solve…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f8e8d7880d8272c0b254d479ad350b0df14c1563.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/0e10b05d9e94dc26baa4400d9e742fa66195e76a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/400f7bbd26369709c183b71d60c5a9dcd000ff74.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/c44053ae4c6e54ab8d3e37cb538e5b17379f3970.png[/img]
[hr][/hr][h2]Endgame Optional Content[/h2] 8-Bit Adventures 2 has many Endgame side-quests, including:

⏱️ A time-hopping mansion with emotional stakes!

🤿 An underwater lair explored via diving suits!

🤖 A grim prison guarded by insane robots!

🏝️ A giant Titan who wanders the World Map!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/50ee1787ffbc3081b8d807d1332337bfa04acbbf.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/b6980142ab82c87903fc0cb8f7d39f0da0790b83.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/c787bedfb8e25d1f2bb59b72a2c869d623d52ea5.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/da2160a5061a9ba7e4003437cd4afc1f01b9e70a.png[/img]
[hr][/hr][h2]Airship Info[/h2] In 8-Bit Adventures 2, the Airship is your high-in-the-sky home!

You can fly across the World Map & reach the Floating Continent, walk on the deck to chat with party members, buy items from an onboard shop, and play the Airship Battle mini-game! 💥

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/41c55f0e0dc68cf20bd6fd366a70a63acc5cf664.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/16b6fe7858ae3515fd6eeb3a4f0adf308819a2dd.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/c3a00697ee6b547aa4ba53b0bb9b2c13dff5c342.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/983370c44d524370a086b5c974890a96917230ca.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Music Sample #8[/h2] Our final music sample before 8-Bit Adventures 2's launch next Tuesday is the exciting, dramatic theme from our popular Gamescom 2020 Trailer! 🎵

This song *does* appear in the game, but its real name and placement is a big spoiler 😉 

[previewyoutube=9vcV8SNPwjs;full][/previewyoutube]
[hr][/hr] And that's it for our showcase series of posts! Thank you very much for taking the time to read through this post, and if you haven't already, please don't forget to wishlist 8-Bit Adventures 2 by clicking the button below. We're just 3 days away, and I'm immensely grateful for everyone's support so far. I know that together, we can make 8-Bit Adventures 2 a success 😊

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

For more information and updates, please:

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 Twitter Showcase Round-Up #2 + Mini-Trailer!
notes.content:
Happy New Year everyone! It's 2023, and that means [b]8-Bit Adventures 2 is launching on PC (Steam & GOG) this month, January 31st![/b] (The console versions are coming later this year)

If you want to support our work and help us have a successful launch, then please consider wishlisting 8-Bit Adventures 2 here on Steam using the button below. It genuinely makes a massive difference.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

But with that out of the way, I'm back again to share another round-up of info, screenshots, and music samples from 8-Bit Adventures 2 that I've been posting on social media (this time from November)!

First up is something brand new - the Panic in the Processor Trailer! It should look very familiar to anyone who's played the 8-Bit Adventures 2 demo.

The Processor is a realm of steam-powered industry - concealed for centuries, now under assault from the Glitch’s clockwork army.

Fight your way through the city, survive a deadly train ride, and reach the great Foundry to put an end to the siege!

[previewyoutube=7EpOk6rxkyY;full][/previewyoutube]

I'll be sharing a new video showcasing 8-Bit Adventures 2 each week in January, so please keep your eyes on Steam or social media!

But you can explore the Processor NOW by playing our Free Demo!

[hr][/hr][h2]Niveus[/h2] Welcome to Niveus – a cozy hideaway in the harsh Frozen North, with indoor heating, sentient snowmen, & a Hot Chocolate item which grants the Regen status! Visiting Niveus is optional, but who could resist the chilly charms of this tundra town 😊

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f50f7567051ad4276622e91528bd1086e30c4495.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Charlie[/h2] Charlie’s a quick-witted, impulsive young man whose big mouth often gets the better of him. One of four orphans saved by the Thief, he grew up idolising her. Now Charlie lives in Pheopolis Castle, & he's spent the last two years training to be just like his hero!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f0f97ba1df56fd44f2afe1d941bd91bc1e661298.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Battle System[/h2] 8-Bit Adventures 2's battles are inspired by Final Fantasy X’s combat system. This means every character takes turns individually & the order of turns is always visible onscreen. Seeing the turn order allows players to plan ahead & think strategically!

Like FFX, we also put a big focus on swapping party members in the midst of battle. More on that in a future post! 😎

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/59c9734f0d1f2be6cbe9a799259f18203087d26a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/e191c4da6f2538679bf5e7df2f5bb5543cf3b1d7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/0e89924095640e762e6e8df589630303bc050d30.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/71ed7aa3cd7e6bc61edfc3d0c122f79dd5201f4d.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Emma[/h2] Emma can seem timid, but she’s a skilled Martial Artist with immense inner strength. An accident claimed both her sight and the lives of her parents, but she was taken in and trained by her Grandpa. Now, Emma yearns to spread her wings & discover her purpose!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/b73945aead92ba9615e6ddae06ebbce8f740f2f6.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Music Preview #3[/h2] This week's music sample is the 8-Bit Adventures 2 boss theme - No Escape! 🎵

This exciting track accompanies many of the 35+ challenging Bosses you'll battle in 8-Bit Adventures 2, and encourages you to give these fights everything you've got! ⚔️

The full 8-Bit Adventures 2 soundtrack features 78 songs, and it launches alongside the PC release on January 31st 2023!

[previewyoutube=5WLt3vKXauI;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr][h2]Omega Burst[/h2] In 8-Bit Adventures 2, you can unleash a powerful Omega Burst attack when the gauge at the bottom of the screen fills up.

In our game there's one gauge for the whole party - so when it's full the player can strategically choose who they want to use it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/a7dfd9830d3b8884357ddcfe412075441cfbeeda.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Robot[/h2] Built by the Computer, the Robot is equipped with state-of-the-art weaponry & tasked with hunting down any anomalies which threaten the safety of the world. A warm, stalwart companion with a logical exterior; he always says whatever’s on his mechanical mind!

FYI, the Robot, Warrior, Thief, and Mage are all characters named by the player in 8-Bit Adventures 2 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/981ea4adad2a312f4738627e578625e4f432680d.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Robot's Parts System[/h2] The most unique character in 8-Bit Adventures 2 is the Robot. He doesn’t use an Attack command or Abilities menu.

Instead, he equips Parts – 3 in total - which determine the attacks he can use. And since Robot has no MP, they can be used infinitely! 🤖

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/248ddabafc32aa7f17c0b5de05f0a1eb606df0b6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/5bb7ad0142578e7216568af8567b0b78999d533e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/c7c130a6c471c6f7d75cf070e251a91c15382cf5.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/ded05af1d263d76da5b6cdaaf96c161e217d02c5.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]The Factory[/h2] The Factory is a bizarre structure, hidden from the world and devoid of humanity 🏭

Run by upbeat robots, it is the seat of power for the mysterious Computer, and is highly coveted by the villainous Glitch. There’s nowhere else quite like it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/52f4a9b78ffe45f5a67d1ad9e56a731cae1dc8fb.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/d836f49aa829bb02d41d83ab7cf062e569df9a0d.png[/img]

[hr][/hr][h2]Personal Skills and Abilities[/h2] Everyone’s got a special skill & the same is true in 8-Bit Adventures 2!

Personal Abilities (like Speed Boost) are passive bonuses unique to each character, while Personal Skills (like Steal) are techniques that can be used in battle & have no MP cost!

Personal Abilities include always getting the first turn, perfect accuracy, & the chance of reflecting damage. While Personal Skills can be stealing items, regenerating MP, or breaking an enemy’s defences!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/b942549e13321a6e5905286866eb57fff4e6ba8b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/6ef8d0b5b008a0f435e13074acb399eef49fa178.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/612fb20e31c98c850e64e19ce7c45d008618f0e4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/3d79634c1929450b19b51deb198d0bfcfa2a97f1.png[/img]

[hr][/hr] And once again, we'll leave it there for now! I'll have another collection of posts like this coming very soon. Thank you very much for taking the time to read through this post, and if you haven't already, please don't forget to wishlist 8-Bit Adventures 2 by clicking the button below 😊

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 PC Release Date + Day of the Devs!
notes.content:
After seven years of hard work and anticipation, I’m overjoyed to announce that [b]8-Bit Adventures 2 will launch on PC (via Steam and GOG) on January 31st, 2023! [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/c5c01efe30deb837964e1f90130a39515d2eaa67.png[/img]

It’s finally happening, everyone!! =D And while I really wanted to hit 2022, at least we’ll only be one month out ;) [b]If you’d like to help make 8-Bit Adventures 2 a success, then please wishlist the game and spread the word to friends or on social media![/b] While it may not seem like it changes much from the outside, it genuinely does make a massive difference for us, and is sincerely appreciated.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/
If you want to inquire about review codes or coverage, you can contact me via josh@criticalgames.com.au 
And please CC Post Horn PR on all messages via: posthornpr@gmail.com 

[b]A gigantic thanks to Day of the Devs, Double Fine, and iam8bit for the opportunity to signal boost this announcement through their wonderful event! [/b]

A unique version of the 8-Bit Adventures 2 demo with Airship and World Map gameplay will be showcased today at Day of the Devs in San Francisco, California, from 3pm until 7pm PDT. Attendance is free, so if you’re in the area, please go and check out this incredible event!

[url=https://www.dayofthedevs.com/events/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/cc5fcd42cf1c1b4d9c50a3bda58611101e7686d8.png[/img][/url]

But that’s not all! The online 8-Bit Adventures 2 demo on Steam and GOG has also been updated to reflect the more polished and finalised state of the full game too. While anyone who’s played the demo before probably won’t notice much of a difference, I wanted to make sure that future demo players would have the best 8-Bit Adventures 2 experience possible – short of playing the full game =) 

I’ve also been doing multiple weekly posts on Twitter and Instagram over the last month, and these will be continuing right through to release (with some of the most exciting ones saved for January!). [b]But I also plan to do regular recaps on Steam, collecting my Twitter posts and sharing them with everyone here - so stay tuned for that too![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/6dc4b2c0b567fa11351d6418069b367392dde772.png[/img]

But what about console players? Well, to reiterate from my previous news post, while Ratalaika Games have been making some great progress on porting, the whole process has taken significantly longer than anticipated due to some unforeseen challenges. When you add console lotcheck on top of that (the approval process to be launched on each platform), the months pile up. 

And so, after talking things over with my team, Ratalaika Games, Post Horn PR (a pro-bono marketing team who are very graciously supporting 8-Bit Adventures 2) and several other developers (whose input I’m very grateful for), [b]I’ve ultimately decided to launch the PC version first,[/b] work on any bug fixes and updates necessary (updating a game is a lot easier on PC than on console), [b]and then release the console versions as soon as everything’s ready. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/488b15417c209b93bbba70e67c67cbf55baf57cf.png[/img]

[b]I sincerely apologise to console players for this delay,[/b] as the plan was always to launch PC and console on the same day. I’ve stuck to and fought for that plan as long as I could (until about the last month and a half); but after speaking further with Ratalaika, it became clear that things had to change. My hope is that console players won’t have to wait too much longer than PC players – and on the bright side, they’ll also receive the Free DLC as part of the base game package, along with any extra fixes and updates for the smoothest and most complete experience.

And just to show you that things are moving ahead, here’s a picture of a (slightly older) development build of 8-Bit Adventures 2 running on a Nintendo Switch console (big thanks to Adrian from Ratalaika for taking this photo for me to share)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/2e4c67b1a970e15d40f4987ebf128e30f91f1e71.jpg[/img]

As for PC players, I know that some of you have been waiting for 8-Bit Adventures 2 since late 2015, and so I didn’t feel it was right to delay any longer. Taking this approach comes with some challenges, but I think it’ll be worth it to get the game in your hands. Thank you very much for your patience & support.

[b]I absolutely cannot wait for you all to get your hands on 8-Bit Adventures 2![/b] There are so many big moments, fun characters, challenging battles, and little details or secrets in this game, and I know Sebastian, Jerram, Sufyan, and I are all desperate to share them with you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/d0407bc9cca4c77ac2ca0d4737cf92b94b058631.png[/img]

[b]8-Bit Adventures 2 is coming to PC and GOG on January 31st 2023,[/b] so please wishlist and spread the word if you’d like to support us! And thank you SO much for all the support that we’ve been given so far!

[i]The people who reach out to me about 8-Bit Adventures 2 are always the most wonderfully kind folks I could ever hope to meet, and I’ve pretty much only received polite and positive messages these past 7 years. Given how unpleasant the internet can be, that’s an incredible achievement – and it’s entirely thanks to all of you! 

Everyone’s kindness has helped me reach the finish line, and for that I am immensely grateful =) [/i]
~Josh

notes.title: August 2022 Update - Filling Everyone In!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! Sorry I’ve been so quiet this year, but thank you very much to everyone who’s checked in with me or offered their support =) I’ve spoken to a lot of you individually on Steam, Twitter, Discord, and so on, but I’ve refrained from doing a major update post because I’ve been waiting until I could announce a release date and start promoting the game’s launch. 

[h3]However, that hasn’t happened, and you all deserve an explanation as to why. So that’s what this update is for![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/26375847173da41de8a0c1dfcf8c4fdb0067a158.gif[/img]

First of all, the good news for anyone who hasn’t heard – [b]8-Bit Adventures 2 is complete.[/b] Every cutscene, every battle, every environment, all 100% finished, polished, and tested. I’ve played through the full game from beginning to end multiple times, and it will take players around 30-40 hours to complete – give or take, due to a wealth of optional content (including a Developer Room with behind-the-scenes info and early assets!). 

I’d also like to thank Benedikt Geierhofer (@RealLeogrim on Twitter) for his help testing the game in recent months! Please check out his upcoming pixel-art RPG “For a Vast Future”, just announced to be releasing in November:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1544000/For_a_Vast_Future/ 

So if 8-Bit Adventures 2 is finished, why is it not out yet? Well, that’s because we’re waiting for the console ports to be ready. Ratalaika Games have been working really hard on the porting process, despite dealing with a lot of challenges over the past year. But unfortunately, 8-Bit Adventures 2 has taken a lot longer than I expected to be ported – partly due to the size of the project and the very large number of plugins used in the game (all of which need to be manually converted). Ratalaika have been making consistent progress and doing their best to get the game ready, but it's one of those jobs that just seems to take as long as it takes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/94cbceb21a744115513a208d28d14b6856e8311d.gif[/img]

Porting is something that I have no control over (it's totally out of my hands), and so I’ve spent the last several months waiting along with all of you. [b]However, I’ve been using this time as effectively as possible.[/b] Not only for testing, but also to make numerous improvements to 8-Bit Adventures 2; combing over every line of dialogue, smoothing any difficulty spikes, testing out more battle configurations and crazy combinations, etc. I’ve now reached the end of that process, but I believe having that extra time to take a deep breath and look over the game as a completed project has resulted in a greatly improved product – in a lot of small ways that really add up. 

[b]Beyond that, I’ve also been starting working on the game’s Free DLC, which has consequently become more substantial than originally planned thanks to this extra time[/b], as well as working on more promotional content (such as mini-trailers highlighting specific sections of the game, and updating the Steam page), and also future top secret plans for releases beyond 8-Bit Adventures 2. While that last one’s a bit premature and relies on 8BA2 selling well, I’m trying to plan ahead so that I can release a game every 2 years, rather than once every 7 years =P

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/6bfb93d4414524262d54026e5af08aa4582267ca.gif[/img]

[b]I know that information is cold-comfort for everyone out there eagerly anticipating the release, but you all deserve an explanation and that’s the honest situation.[/b] I’ll be providing updates as I’m given news myself, and once we've passed certification I'll be shouting a release date from the rooftops!

But on the very bright side, 8-Bit Adventures 2 is finally done and, in my opinion, it’s turned out to be a great game and something really special. Obviously I’m the most biased person in the world when it comes to this project, but I’ve also been taking a hyper-critical eye to the game for the past seven years, so I think I can at least say that anyone who loves JRPGs like I do will have a lot of fun. [b]I’m really, really proud of 8-Bit Adventures 2 – and so grateful to everyone on our team who made it possible![/b]

There’s not much I can do to tide you over while we all wait, and I know a lot of people don't want any spoilers beyond what I've shown so far. BUT for anyone who’s interested, [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=So-jiP2SWUk]here’s a sneak-peek at the “Adventures in Anbu” mini-trailer[/url][/b] – focusing on a small section of the game where you battle a legendary Samurai and his undead army in a distant land inspired by medieval Japan. The video’s unlisted, so it’s just a bonus for anyone who read this =) 

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=So-jiP2SWUk][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/467a0422507b4362b76e5d534959d83fa2134bbc.png[/img][/url]

[i]Anyway, I just wanted to make sure that everyone knew what was going on, and where we're at. Essentially, I'm waiting like everyone else now. But I'm also trying to plan and think ahead so that - if 8-Bit Adventures 2 does well - I'll be able to provide you guys with a steady stream of fun content in future. But for now, thank you very much for all of your support; it really means the world to me! [/i]
~Josh

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 at Steam Next Fest Feb 2022!
notes.content:
I'm thrilled to announce that 8-Bit Adventures 2 is participating in Steam's latest Next Fest event - and to celebrate this, [b]the 8-Bit Adventures 2 Demo has received a big update![/b] What does it do? Let's dive in!

For anyone who's already played the previous demo, this latest version features all of the same content. You can once again choose between playing through the game's Prologue, battling your way through an exciting Dungeon, and exploring a Town with a hidden boss battle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f657334118884ff0517d9be5dd5f3d3fccb8a44a.gif[/img]

However, this latest update includes a TON of changes, fixes, and improvements. Simply put, this update makes the demo run and play like the final, release-level product! But how about some specifics?

[h2]What's New in the Demo?[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]A massive performance boost[/b], bringing the game up to near rock-solid 60fps performance (this boost accounts for most of the increase in file size, in case anyone was curious!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/920058c191da252dfd2a1dbc0c53447070b7eaa2.gif[/img]
[*][b]Dozens and dozens (and dozens) of bug fixes[/b] which make battles run smoother and ensure everything works as intended. And the game's balance has been improved too!
[*][b]Enhanced UI elements[/b], such as indicating to the player what percentage their HP/MP is currently at through the use of colour, displaying a character's Max HP/MP when you go to use a restorative item in battle, as well as the addition of an icon which indicates which enemies have rare steal-able items which you don't currently possess!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/183df24c4e2829f3303e1bb7dfafa6cc38bc18a0.gif[/img]
[*]Improved support for high refresh-rate monitors.
[*][b]A Quick Menu button[/b] which allows the player to bring up a specific menu with just one press. The exact menu that's brought up can be customised in the Options menu.
[*][b]The Tutorial sub-menu[/b], which details the game's mechanics, offering an easy refresher if the player ever forgets something. More tutorials are unlocked as you progress through the game.
[*][b]A new Sprint Mode option[/b] that allows the player to choose between Holding a button down to sprint, or Toggling running/walking speed with the press of a button. I'm a Hold mode kind of guy myself, but options are all about figuring out what works best for you!
[*][b]A Battle Status menu[/b] that can be brought up during combat to display a complete summary of the player's party (detailing Equipment, Augments, Statuses, etc.), designed to be a handy reference.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f54891642a0d8e96a96336b61164aefb0c7721b3.gif[/img]
[*][b]Improved Ability/Item descriptions[/b] (and animations in a handful of cases) which clarify details which may have been more obtuse or poorly handled in past releases.
[*][b]Scrolling text in battle![/b] The text displayed at the top of the screen during battle now scrolls as player/enemy actions play out, providing more relevant details. For example, say that there's an attack which deals damage and poisons an enemy. Some flavour text will appear about the attack, followed by a description of the damage dealt. But then the text will scroll down to also state that the enemy was poisoned. This is much more elegant than before.
[*][b]The Equipment and Augment menus now display character portraits[/b], making the currently selected character easier to discern at a glance. Additionally, Shop menus now also feature character graphics for the same reason. 
[*]The game will now pop up "Immune" text if an enemy (or ally) is unable to be inflicted by a particular Status Ailment. 
[*][b]If you get a Game Over, you can now choose to Open the Menu before retrying a battle[/b], allowing you to change up your Equipment/Augments, or heal a character with low HP/MP. This way, you don't have to reload & re-watch any cutscenes if you want to change up your approach to combat.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/ade21325c9cd4b97293c6f872b80991ef96df6d9.gif[/img]

[b]Honestly, I could go on forever[/b] - like how the Warrior's Strong Attack now has an increased Critical Hit chance, the Exit Game menu now allows you to load a save file without returning to the main menu, the healing sub-menu now takes up less space and leaves the currently selected column of the Item menu visible, if an enemy has two damaging Status Ailments affecting them at once the damage numbers will no longer overlap, etc. Truth be told, I doubt I could even remember *everything* that's been fixed or changed haha. 

So while on the surface this will seem like a very familiar demo to long-time fans, [b]the goal was to raise the overall polish and quality-of-life features to the standard of the full, release-level game.[/b]

[h2]Development Progress Update![/h2]
On that note, while I can't give as much of an update as I wanted to (and I know you all want), I *can* talk about where the game is at! 

I probably have a little under a month of work left on the game myself (although I naturally won't stop testing until release). 8-Bit Adventures 2 is playable from beginning to end - with every battle fully functional and all the gameplay content tested and polished. I've just got to finish up on some cutscene work for the end-game side quests and epilogue, as well as put together the hidden Developer Room (that's been left 'till last as it's extraneous to the core experience). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/3535063b8d8ebc9376c1f464bbe60bef43769988.png[/img]

In case you missed it, while I originally thought that 8-Bit Adventures 2 would be a 20 hour game during development, [b]it's turned out to be a jam-packed 30+ hour adventure (including side quests). [/b]And none of that time is spent on filler or grinding; I've tried to make the game wall-to-wall content, so it's been a really big project. 

So despite how quiet I've been recently, things have been going really well! [b]I'm at the point where a lot of things are beyond my direct control, so please bear with me; because I'll be delivering every bit of news to you the moment I'm allowed to deliver it![/b]

[h2]Some BIG Thank Yous[/h2]
First of all, [b]I'd like to give a MASSIVE thank you to Sufyan Noor, our wonderful programmer who's implemented all of the above ideas with me.[/b] He's done an AMAZING job, and I'm really grateful for all the work he's put in. No matter how hard the challenge I pose to him, he always finds a way to pull it off!

Secondly, a TON of gratitude to Peter Ruibal, otherwise known as fmoo on the Something Classic Discord server. He helped me with a last-minute Steam issue that threatened to derail this demo, completely out of the kindness of his heart. So thank you very much Pete! [b]He's working on an upcoming JRPG called Quartet, which I *highly* recommend you check out because the team behind it are some of the nicest, smartest, most talented developers I've ever met![/b]
 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1307960/Quartet/

Finally, I wanted to thank everyone who's played the demo in previous years. And especially those who gave feedback! [b]There are several items on the list above which I added to the game *specifically* because of player feedback. [/b]Even if something doesn't end up being implemented, I do take everything on-board, [b]so thank you all for taking the time to share your thoughts with me![/b] We're at such a late stage now that not much else will be able to change, but I'll definitely be updating the game post-launch so please do feel free to offer feedback if anything stands out to you =D

[h2]Wrapping Up[/h2]
If you've played the demo before, this update might not seem like a big deal - for which I apologise. I didn't want to spoil any more of the game than I've already put out there. And I also know a lot of people haven't played the demo before, so I didn't want to take development time away from the main game to build a whole new demo (which would've probably taken 3 weeks to a month). 

However, everything that's been added in this new update demonstrates a giant step forward for 8-Bit Adventures 2. [b]We're at the point now where the game plays like a final, release-level product - even better than I originally envisioned - and that's incredibly exciting to me![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/85d93b57e815191065350a322eeef875ac8da203.gif[/img]

And don't forget to check out all the other amazing demos included in Steam Next Fest! If you're interested in 8-Bit Adventures 2, I'd say games like [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1544000/For_a_Vast_Future/]For a Vast Future[/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1099640/Jack_Move/]Jack Move[/url], and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1848070/Absinthia/]Absinthia[/url] might be right up your alley =) 

[i]Anyway, my journey nears its end, and yours is soon to begin - so please keep your eyes peeled for news. I'll probably give everyone an update on porting progress next time I post (just to keep you all in the loop), and then the one after that will be the release date announcement - followed by the actual release! =D[/i]
~Josh

[b]P.S. I'd sincerely appreciate it if you could add 8-Bit Adventures 2 to your wishlist, as this genuinely helps us out (particularly during Steam Next Fest and at launch)![/b] Our most adorable enemy - a puffball named Eek - *really* wants you to do it =P

tags.feature: [b]A massive performance boost[/b], bringing the game up to near rock-solid 60fps performance (this boost accounts for most of the increase in file size, in case anyone was curious!)

tags.bug: [b]Dozens and dozens (and dozens) of bug fixes[/b] which make battles run smoother and ensure everything works as intended.

tags.balance_change: And the game's balance has been improved too!

tags.feature: [b]Enhanced UI elements[/b], such as indicating to the player what percentage their HP/MP is currently at through the use of colour, displaying a character's Max HP/MP when you go to use a restorative item in battle, as well as the addition of an icon which indicates which enemies have rare steal-able items which you don't currently possess!
Improved support for high refresh-rate monitors.
[b]A Quick Menu button[/b] which allows the player to bring up a specific menu with just one press. The exact menu that's brought up can be customised in the Options menu.
[b]The Tutorial sub-menu[/b], which details the game's mechanics, offering an easy refresher if the player ever forgets something. More tutorials are unlocked as you progress through the game.

[b]A new Sprint Mode option[/b] that allows the player to choose between Holding a button down to sprint, or Toggling running/walking speed with the press of a button. I'm a Hold mode kind of guy myself, but options are all about figuring out what works best for you!
[b]A Battle Status menu[/b] that can be brought up during combat to display a complete summary of the player's party (detailing Equipment, Augments, Statuses, etc.), designed to be a handy reference.
[b]Improved Ability/Item descriptions[/b] (and animations in a handful of cases) which clarify details which may have been more obtuse or poorly handled in past releases.

[b]Scrolling text in battle![/b] The text displayed at the top of the screen during battle now scrolls as player/enemy actions play out, providing more relevant details. For example, say that there's an attack which deals damage and poisons an enemy. Some flavour text will appear about the attack, followed by a description of the damage dealt. But then the text will scroll down to also state that the enemy was poisoned. This is much more elegant than before.

[b]The Equipment and Augment menus now display character portraits[/b], making the currently selected character easier to discern at a glance. Additionally, Shop menus now also feature character graphics for the same reason.

tags.bug: The game will now pop up "Immune" text if an enemy (or ally) is unable to be inflicted by a particular Status Ailment.

tags.feature: [b]If you get a Game Over, you can now choose to Open the Menu before retrying a battle[/b], allowing you to change up your Equipment/Augments, or heal a character with low HP/MP. This way, you don't have to reload & re-watch any cutscenes if you want to change up your approach to combat.

tags.balance_change: the Warrior's Strong Attack now has an increased Critical Hit chance

tags.feature: the Exit Game menu now allows you to load a save file without returning to the main menu
the healing sub-menu now takes up less space and leaves the currently selected column of the Item menu visible

tags.bug: if an enemy has two damaging Status Ailments affecting them at once the damage numbers will no longer overlap

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 is Coming to Consoles + Discounts and More!
notes.content:
[h2]Console Announcement Sale![/h2]

As a special promotion, from 10AM on October 13th (today) through to 10AM on October 20th (Pacific Time), you can get 8-Bit Adventures 1 at 60% off! That means you can own it for just $4 USD! You can also get the fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD), or the Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/370300/8Bit_Adventures_The_Forgotten_Journey_Remastered_Edition/
Additionally, my most recent game Tales Across Time is also participating in the sale, making an already cheap game even cheaper! You can now get it 20% off - that's just $2.39 USD!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/461710/Tales_Across_Time/
As I've said before, these discounts won't get any lower in the future, so now's the time to buy if you're interested in checking these games out and supporting the final phase of development on 8-Bit Adventures 2!

[h2]8-Bit Adventures 2 Console Announcements[/h2]

I’ve been pretty vague on the topic of consoles for 8-Bit Adventures 2 for a while now, [i]but no more![/i]

[previewyoutube=NQMPDiH7kho;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]I’m ecstatic to reveal that 8-Bit Adventures 2 will be available on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation®5 (PS5™), PlayStation®4 (PS4™), Xbox Series X|S, and Xbox One consoles – simultaneously alongside the Steam and GOG releases for PC! [/b]

After our game was showcased at gamescom last year, we received a tremendous number of requests to bring 8-Bit Adventures 2 to consoles. While it’s added a *lot* of extra work to a project that’s already been in development for over 5 years, [b]my goal is to make sure that *everyone* can enjoy this classic JRPG adventure – no matter where you prefer to play.[/b] So I sincerely hope that fans on every platform are going to be really happy about this news! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/18d7102f705e12c72879d12e93f59db4078f465b.png[/img]
[i]Look at all those logos! ;) [/i]

The console versions are being ported by the incredibly talented porting company (and publisher) Ratalaika Games. To put it simply, RPG Maker MV games like 8-Bit Adventures 2 are tremendously difficult to bring to consoles, and without Ratalaika Games a simultaneous release would not have been possible. The technical wizards there have developed their own tools to achieve this, and it even allows me to keep a hand on the wheel – fixing bugs, testing the console versions, and developing any future content updates. 

[b]It was fan support that has ultimately allowed us to take this project further than I ever imagined. I’m genuinely thrilled to be bringing 8-Bit Adventures 2 to every major console platform[/b], and I hope the Nintendo, PlayStation®, and Xbox communities will enjoy discovering the grand, character-driven story, dynamic turn-based battles, and ‘familiar yet fresh’ experience that awaits them in this epic new adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/fd56d3183b78ea856be7a12c91722836a7736d4e.gif[/img]

For PC players, I realise that all of this console talk probably hasn’t been the most exciting news. Console work has taken up a *ton* of my time this year (along with something ambitious that I took a chance on because I felt it would help the game, but sadly didn’t pan out. I am currently unable to elaborate on this), and it has taken that time away from development on the game. [b]And for that, I apologise – PC players are the ones who have been waiting the longest, and I fully recognise that![/b] But just to be clear, there’s not a finished PC build that I’m holding back from release until the console versions are done or anything crazy like that. There’s just one core build that I’m trying to complete, and each release spirals out from that. 

I’m not actually allowed to announce a release date until certain obligations have been fulfilled (and I’ve learnt a lot about best release practices and timings), so there’ll probably only be a month’s notice before the game is released. What I *can* tell you, though, is that [b]we currently have 21 hours worth of completely finished and finalised 8-Bit Adventures 2 – along with a ton of quality-of-life changes and under-the-hood improvements since the last demo was released.[/b] I’ve also got some more big announcements to make in the not-too-distant future (one of which in particular I think will make people very happy), so please stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/0f114ed51141ae87670edd2eb96b8e62cf47d841.png[/img]

On a personal note, I will admit that this year’s been…exhausting haha. There’s been so much to keep track of – both in terms of development, and everything else surrounding the game – that it’s felt tremendously overwhelming. Probably a little too much for one person in retrospect XD At the end of the day, I’m a creative who likes to tell stories and design fun game mechanics, so the business, marketing, and management aspects of development over the last year and a half have required a lot of learning. Going back into lockdown for the past several months definitely hasn’t helped matters either haha! 

It’s been an incredibly tough couple of years for everyone, though, and I’ve really had it easy - so I’m saying this to explain where I’m currently at, rather than to complain. After all, while it may be more work for me, it’s good news for the game! I’m lucky that every time I work on and play 8-Bit Adventures 2, I still feel genuinely excited and enjoy the experience very much – despite how tedious game development can sometimes get. Crafting the best possible experience for all of you is what keeps me plugging away, and I’m so, so happy with how the game has turned out. And now that we’re coming to consoles, it really feels like we’re not leaving anything on the table. [b]By the time 8-Bit Adventures 2 releases, I’ll have done literally everything I possibly can to make the game a success – and that’s a good feeling =D[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/01e2b0225d07bd7609fd15d5b03a8fab876aaf39.png[/img]

I’ve also been thinking a lot about what comes next. Put simply, I have no intention of doing a 5-6 year project again (I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone haha XD), and so I’ve been toying with two ideas that would provide content-rich experiences and keep me doing what I do best (making RPGs), but would also allow me to release two full games within a 2 and a half year window. I’m also planning at least one free content update for 8-Bit Adventures 2 after it’s released, which I will hopefully be able to begin development of at some point during the porting process (I’d like to release it around a month after launch). This is an idea I’ve had for several years now, and I think it’s a fun basis for optional, bonus story content. 

But sticking firmly in the present, [b]I’ve just revamped the old Critical Games Youtube Channel.[/b] It now has current trailers and branding, [b]as well as a playlist with over 21 minutes of Music Samples from the 8-Bit Adventures 2 OST![/b] All future 8-Bit Adventures 2 videos will be uploaded here, so please check it out and subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/user/CriticalGamesDev

[url=https://www.youtube.com/user/CriticalGamesDev][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/a652f8e2c6fa7d672541c13597dacf731933da55.png[/img][/url]

[i]Anyway, the future is looking very bright! If you’re a long-time follower of 8-Bit Adventures 2, thank you so, so much for your support – I’m sincerely, immensely grateful. And if you’ve only just discovered 8-Bit Adventures 2, then welcome! I’m over-the-moon that you’re taking an interest in the game and I can’t wait to hear your thoughts =D Talk to everyone again soon! [/i]
~Josh

notes.title: July Update - Discounts + 8-Bit Adventures 2 at DreamHack Beyond TODAY!
notes.content:
Hi everyone! [b]I’m excited to reveal that 8-Bit Adventures 2 is a part of DreamHack Beyond – and the event begins TODAY![/b]

[b][url=https://dreamhack.com/beyond/]https://dreamhack.com/beyond/[/url][/b]

[b]What is DreamHack Beyond?[/b] It’s a fully digital, online convention that’s styled like a point-and-click adventure game. It features demos, cosplay, tournaments, game booths, and even a story-driven adventure – all rolled into a unique online multiplayer experience with a gorgeous, Cartoon Network-inspired art style! Seriously, I’ve gone hands on with my booth area, and I’m incredibly impressed with what they’ve built.

[previewyoutube=9rOyf-HaVdY;full][/previewyoutube]
If you like JRPGs and chatting with quirky NPCs in games, I think you’ll really enjoy this. [b]In fact, I’m an NPC in DreamHack Beyond too![/b] So you can chat to "me" about 8-Bit Adventures 2 [i]inside[/i] the game ;) 

Speaking of which, you can find my doppelganger at the 8-Bit Adventures 2 booth in Hive 3!

[b]To join the event, all you need to do is claim your FREE ticket here: [/b]
[b][url=https://dreamhack.com/tickets/dhb1]https://dreamhack.com/tickets/dhb1[/url][/b]

[b]I am incredibly grateful to have been invited to show 8-Bit Adventures 2 at DreamHack Beyond, and I honestly think this is one online convention you won’t want to miss.[/b] Especially if you’re currently in lockdown like I am here in Australia!

[h2]DreamHack Beyond Sale![/h2]
To celebrate the event, I’m also running some discounts! From 10AM on July 24th through to 10AM on July 31st (Pacific Time), you can get 8-Bit Adventures 1 at 60% off! That means you can own it for just $4 USD! You can also get the fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD), or the Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/370300/8Bit_Adventures_The_Forgotten_Journey_Remastered_Edition/

Additionally, my most recent game Tales Across Time is also participating in the sale, making an already cheap game even cheaper! You can now get it 20% off - that's just $2.39 USD!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/461710/Tales_Across_Time/

As I've said before, these discounts won't get any lower in the future, so now's the time to buy if you're interested in checking these games out and supporting the final phase of development on 8-Bit Adventures 2!

[h2]General Updates[/h2]
I’m very sorry for the radio silence; I haven’t wanted to do any big updates for a while, as I’ve been working at a really good pace. That said, I’m still responding to everyone that leaves me a comment here or on social media, and am active on Twitter ([url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url]) and our [url=https://discord.gg/aKf2tr4]Discord channel[/url]. But I know plenty of people don’t look at those, so I’ll be sharing some of the updates I’ve made there in this post.

But just before that, I apologise for how quiet I’ve been on announcements this year. A[b] whole big string of them is on the horizon[/b] (lots and lots of things I’ve been trying to plan and organise finally coming to fruition), [b]but I’m trying to find the best time to do so.[/b] 8-Bit Adventures 2’s development is going really well, though! 

I'm waiting until the game is actually finished to announce a release date, as the last thing I want to do is disappoint anyone again. But I know how frustrating that is for all of you – [b]and I don’t for a moment take your patience and support for granted.[/b] I’m incredibly lucky to have such wonderful people looking forward to 8-Bit Adventures 2, and I’ll always be upfront and honest about things whenever I’m asked =) 

[b]However, I can say that I have 15 hours of completely finished, polished, bug tested, finalised game - with the remaining hours partially finished[/b] (I'm predicting around 23-24 hours, depending on the player - but a lot of the late game content is a little more free-flowing and player driven, as you have the freedom of an Airship, and can tackle a bunch of sidequests, so it's easier on development - compared to the more scripted, heavily directed content that comprises the bulk of the game). [b]So the last few months have been extremely productive![/b] I’m honestly feeling a bit exhausted haha, but I feel like I’m making constant, significant progress, so that’s a great feeling =D 

Anyway, onto sharing some of those updates!

[b]First up, let’s look at a new addition to 8-Bit Adventures 2: the Battle Status Window![/b] With the push of a button, you can view the whole party's details in a handy little window; Stats, Equipment, Augments, and current Status effects (as well as how long those Status effects have left before they disappear)! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/f54891642a0d8e96a96336b61164aefb0c7721b3.gif[/img]

When you have a six or seven character party, this window can really help you stay on top of who has what, and will help you decide which allies to swap in or out.  

[b]Next up is the Autosave system![/b] While not the most visually exciting thing to show, it’s essential to a modern RPG. So whatever happens, you’ll always have a back-up! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/e6b16863a63b49a431ad97891dac8d3b59ab2672.png[/img]

[b]For something a little bit different, here’s an update I posted about running around in the large, neon-lit City of Sounds[/b] - one of the 29 dungeons featured in 8-Bit Adventures 2. Here you'll face electrified guitarists, enemy-buffing backup drummers, and tone-deaf singers with killer vocals!

Unfortunately, I can't share this one directly as the GIF file is too big for Steam, but you can check out the tweet here: https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU/status/1396106620954824711

[b]And finally, back in May, 8-Bit Adventures 2's performance got a big boost![/b] The game now has a rock-solid 60fps frame rate, and this has made a tremendous difference to the feel of the game. For example, enemies spotting you on the World Map used to cause a lag spike, but not anymore! Note: I had to compress and cut this one a little to fit it on Steam - sorry about that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/920058c191da252dfd2a1dbc0c53447070b7eaa2.gif[/img]

[b]All of these improvements are thanks to our amazing programmer Sufyan Noor, so a round of applause for him please![/b] He’s doing amazing work adding this last coat of polish to the technical side of the game, and implementing the Quality of Life elements I’ve designed. 

[b]Lastly, I also wanted to share this awesome, adorable piece of fan art that Starzee posted on our Discord![/b] It's the 8-Bit Adventures 2 cast if they were made into plushies, and I absolutely LOVE it (and want to buy them haha)! Thanks so much for creating it and letting me share your work Starzee =D

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30941067/3cd280d5467ac9eb3f56437d1468e28820dfa39c.png[/img]

[i]I'm sorry I don't have more to announce, but there's a lot to come ([b]I've got announcements related to seven different companies[/b] in the long-term!). I'm so, so incredibly grateful for all of your support - every comment truly means a lot to me. But please, [b]don't forget to check out DreamHack Beyond[/b] - I'm very grateful to be a part of it, and I genuinely think it's going to be something special. I'm looking forward to hopping on myself! =D[/i]
~Josh
