notes.title: Updates, Delays, and Sales – Oh My!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/55903124064f766fe9db55ea5cc842513df230ca.gif[/img]

Lots of news this time around, including a brand new content update for the 8-Bit Adventures 2 Demo! 

But let's get the business stuff out of the way first:

[h1][b][u]Weeklong Sale Discounts[/u][/b][/h1]

For this week only (until 10:00 AM on April 16th Pacific Time), you can get [b][i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] at 60% off![/b] That means you can own it for just [b]$4 USD![/b] You can also get the [b]fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD)[/b], or the [b]Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)![/b]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/370300
Additionally, my most recent game [b][i]Tales Across Time[/i] is also participating in the sale[/b], making an already cheap game even [b]cheaper![/b] You can now get it 20% off - [b]that's just $2.39 USD!![/b]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710
These [b]discounts won't get any lower[/b] in the future, so get 'em while they're hot! ;)

And remember, [b]every purchase goes towards 8-Bit Adventures 2's development.[/b] As many of you know, I am funding development myself, [b]so any and all support is greatly appreciated![/b]

[h1][b][u]8-Bit Adventures 2 Delay[/u][/b][/h1]

Okay, so let’s tackle the elephant in the room – it’s Early 2018 Josh, so [b]where’s the release?[/b] Well, as you might have guessed by this point, 8-Bit Adventures 2 will not be releasing in Early 2018. No excuses; we’re simply not ready and the game is not finished. And I really can’t do anything else but apologise for this.

Honestly, there’s probably no one more eager to release 8-Bit Adventures 2 than I am, because the game is essentially my livelihood. Until that’s released (and hopefully sells well…wink, wink; nudge, nudge =P) I don’t have an income. But, of course, [b]there’s no way I’m going to release an unfinished game[/b] – that doesn’t work out well for anyone.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/570ef259794fe3dbd94f33331766dfa6eb16f8b1.gif[/img]

Now, I do think it will be sooner rather than later and I have an estimate of when I think it will release (which is less than 6 months away). But I don’t want to say anything specific until I have an exact, locked-in, unchangeable date to give you. [b]It *will* be released before the end of this year though;[/b] that I can promise you unequivocally.  

But [b]I am sincerely sorry that I have failed to meet this deadline[/b] and can only ask that you continue to support us as we finally (*finally*) approach release. 

[h1][b][u]New Content Update for Demo[/u][/b][/h1]

In lighter news, you guys have definitely been doing that! Over 1000 people have downloaded and played the 8-Bit Adventures 2 First Look Demo, and nearly 1500 people have added the full game to their wishlist! This shows an intention to purchase the game on launch, and it makes me incredibly optimistic about 8-Bit Adventures 2’s chances for success (which in turn will allow me to continue making games in future). So thank you very much to everyone who has played the demo or added the game to their wishlist.     

In fact, player feedback has provided lots of valuable information, so I sincerely appreciate all of the responses I’ve received. By far the most common request I’ve seen is for [b]the addition of a ‘Run’ button.[/b] Your feedback convinced me that this was the right way to go, and not only has it been implemented in the full game, but [b]I’ve updated the demo to include this as well.[/b] The demo also now includes new tweaks to the battle system, [b]a new bonus boss, a new playable character, and a silly alternate ending![/b] So if you’re in the mood, I hope you’ll check it out =D

Note: At the time of writing, [b]the demo has not yet been updated.[/b] I’ll remove this note once it has, but Steam should let you know when the update is downloaded. I apologise for the delay; just trying to be thorough and make sure I haven’t accidentally broken anything!

[h1][b][u]Behind the Scenes: Music Samples, Art, & More![/u][/b][/h1]

So then, what’s going on behind-the-scenes? Well, I am very happy to announce that I have commissioned a professional comic book artist to draw a piece of promotional art (the “box” art, essentially) for 8-Bit Adventures 2. I won’t say who it is just yet, but the artist and image should be revealed sometime next month, so please stay tuned. Needless to say, I’m very excited to see it!

Beyond that, with enemies, battle backgrounds, and tiles done (among many other things), Jerram Fahey (the artist) is hard at work tackling the remaining Battle Animations – and trust me, that’s a long list! The seven playable characters alone have around 98 abilities in total. And then when you add enemies and items into that mix, well…there are lots of crashes, bangs, booms, and whams that need animating. 

He’s also working on something that I’ve been hoping to do since before development began – something that will be used to enhance a handful of key cutscenes. Those of you who’ve played Ninja Gaiden on NES might have an inkling of what I’m talking about ;)

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/55903124064f766fe9db55ea5cc842513df230ca.gif[/img]

The soundtrack surpassed 50 songs last week, and we’re still not done! Carfonu (the composer) has been working very hard, and I really can’t wait for you all to hear his work in full – the variety of sounds and styles he’s managed to create, despite the limitations of the NES (Famicom technically) sound chip, is incredible. Have a listen to some new samples!

[h1]Bruneus[/h1] https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/bruneus-sample 

[url=https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/bruneus-sample][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/d932555134d43e62822c2211a506bd83b02f8f48.gif[/img][/url]

[h1]Mystery Theme (What will it be?!)[/h1] https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/mystery-theme-sample

[url=https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/mystery-theme-sample][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/271ccde5dd3a69147deea385c203c2d955b0515d.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Anbu City Theme[/h1] https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/anbu-city-sample

[url=https://soundcloud.com/8bitadventures2/anbu-city-sample][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/ac15052582f449a89815c3c724107f29c4b5b728.gif[/img][/url]

As for me (Josh - I design/develop the game), I’ve been making steady progress. Fun fact: I’ve apparently written over 100,000 words of dialogue so far, which is pretty crazy to think! This past week, I’ve been finishing up the continent of Anbu – which is the Japanese-inspired area you might have glimpsed in some trailers and screenshots. The main dungeon here is an old, ruined pagoda (fortress) with a heavily guarded exterior and 8-storey tower. It’s a fairly lengthy dungeon, and has some cool moments (like using Robot to slam through the gates leading up to the tower’s entrance while fighting off undead soldiers and ninja), so it was a lot of fun to design!  

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/a44f11950dc4fc88aab9ec6492c1a5bd66db7034.gif[/img]

I’ve also started putting together the Instruction Manual. While it’s not quite the same as the old days, everyone will have access to a full colour, 25+ page manual when the game is launched – complete with silly jokes, concept artwork, information about the world, and even some useful information!

You can read a ‘Press Release’ that I made in the same style on the 8-Bit Adventures 2 website (www.8bitadventures2.com), but here are a couple of sample pages from the final manual if you’re curious. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/5b00da126a2f717cdc5a003f0043b283cc381d83.png[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30941067/8428da87f8a2cc0550618aa2f982f232c92baacd.png[/img]

[h1][b][u]That's All Folks![/u][/b][/h1]

But anyway, that’s really all I can say for now. Again, I sincerely apologise that the game is not available yet, but I hope you’ll stick with me in this final stretch. 

And please stay tuned for more updates! I always post 8-Bit Adventures 2 news here on Steam (including on the new 8-Bit Adventures 2 Steam Page!), but [b]I also highly recommend following [/b][url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter, as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news! [/b]

[b]You can also check out the [/b][url=www.8bitadventures2.com]8-Bit Adventures 2 Website[/url] for more info and screenshots (including our new Dev Blog), or check Facebook at: https://www.facebook.com/CriticalGamesDev

[b][i]Let me know what you think about the demo updates!~[/i][/b]
Josh

www.8bitadventures2.com

http://store.steampowered.com/app/733110/8Bit_Adventures_2/

But seeing as this is an update post, I wanted to leave you with a little something extra - [b]a new screenshot![/b] And this one might look very familiar to players of 8-Bit Adventures 1 ;) 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/37112825402e2b2e3c5830bc408e6509f905f06f.gif[/img]

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 2 Steam Page Launch + First Look Demo!
notes.content:
I am very excited to announce that the 8-Bit Adventures 2 Steam Page has officially launched, alongside a special ‘First Look’ Demo! 

http://store.steampowered.com/app/733110
Additionally, the official 8-Bit Adventures 2 website is live, alongside a brand new Trailer. Check them out below:

[b]Website:[/b] www.8bitadventures2.com  

[b]Trailer:[/b] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z5bOGBbRHMQ 
[h1][b]Demo and Release Delay[/b][/h1]

[b]The ‘First Look’ Demo will give you an early taste of the turn-based JRPG action![/b] But I should say, the game is constantly improving and evolving every day, so the demo’s content may not be exactly the same as the final version, and it’s almost certain that any problems with the demo will be fixed by the time of release. With that said, [b]I absolutely welcome any and all feedback and would love to hear what you think[/b] – whether it’s via email or via the Steam Community here. 

8-Bit Adventures 2 is entirely self-funded and is by far the longest and most difficult development cycle I’ve ever tackled – and it still has quite a way to go. While we’ve all tried our best, I must unfortunately announce that 8-Bit Adventures 2 will not be releasing in 2017, and now sits under a vague, unsatisfying [b]‘Early 2018’[/b] release window. I sincerely apologise if this disappoints anyone, but we’re all committed to making this game something truly special and it simply won’t be ready this year. Hopefully the content I’ve released today will help to tide you over!

[h1][b]Who are We?[/b][/h1]

But I shouldn’t get ahead of myself – [b]who are “we”?[/b] Well, my name is Joshua Hallaran and I’m an Australian indie developer, working under the company name Critical Games since 2011. Best known for creating RPGs on the PC - notably 8-Bit Adventures & Tales Across Time - I am currently hard at work developing 8-Bit Adventures 2. But thankfully I’m not alone! I’m working with three very talented freelancers: 

[b]Artist - Jerram Fahey[/b] – who is the source of all the amazing artwork, both in-game and out, and might just be a wizard given what he can do with the NES colour palette!

[b]Composer – Carfonu[/b] - who makes all of the incredible NES-accurate music for the 8-Bit Adventures games. It’s just another reason you should watch the trailer and play the demo, but be careful – I can’t get some of these songs out of my head!

[b]Programmer - Dr “iBolt” Dhoom[/b] - who programmed the entire battle system and must be getting *extremely* tired of bug reports! 

[h1][b]Want to Help?[/b][/h1]

If you’re brand new to 8-Bit Adventures, then welcome! Or if you’re a returning player who’s been reading my recent updates, thanks for sticking with me. [b]If you’d like to support the game[/b], then please add it to your Wishlist and consider purchasing my previous games: [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/370300]8-Bit Adventures 1[/url] or [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710]Tales Across Time[/url]. As I said before, [b]the game is self-funded, so those sales help out quite a bit.[/b] In fact, it’s thanks to the players of those games that 8-Bit Adventures 2 exists at all!

Beyond that, [b]please spread the word![/b] Indie games like mine thrive on word of mouth, so if you know someone who loves JRPGs, pixel art, chip-tunes, or a good story and characters – particularly someone with an affinity for the NES, SNES, or PS1 eras – then please let them know about 8-Bit Adventures 2!

But that’s all from me for now! I hope that everyone enjoys the new demo/trailer/website, and that you’ll look forward to the final release next year. If you’d like to keep up with all the latest news, either check back on the [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/733110]8-Bit Adventures 2 Steam Page[/url] or follow [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter. 

And if you want a reminder for when the game is released, [b]please don’t forget to add it to your Steam Wishlist![/b]

Thank you all so much for your time and I hope to post again soon.
~Have fun! ːOrbGetWarriorː ːOrbGetThiefː ːOrbGetMageː

notes.title: 8-Bit Adventures 60% Off + 8-Bit 2 Battle Animations Preview!
notes.content:
Wow, time really gets away. I can't believe it's already been two months since my last post! If you missed it back in June, check here for an in-depth look at the Battle System of the upcoming 8-Bit Adventures 2: http://steamcommunity.com/games/8bitadventures/announcements/detail/1337981636744892152 But if you're up-to-date (or simply don't care), then let's get onto the new stuff!

[h1][b][u]Weeklong Sale Discounts[/u][/b][/h1]

First up, we've got some exciting discounts! For this week only (starting August 21st), you can get [b][i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] at 60% off![/b] That means you can own it for just [b]$4 USD![/b] You can also get the [b]fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD)[/b], or the [b]Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)![/b]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/370300
Additionally, my most recent game [b][i]Tales Across Time[/i] is also participating in the sale[/b], making an already cheap game even [b]cheaper![/b] For the [b]first time ever[/b], you get it 20% off - [b]that's just $2.39 USD!![/b]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710
In the last two sales, I noted that the [b]discounts wouldn't get any lower[/b]. However, after much thought, I decided to increase the discount on Tales Across Time, as that's only ever had one price reduction and I felt it was time to go lower. I sincerely apologise if anyone feels misled, but I can confirm that [b]the discounts on 8-Bit Adventures have not, and will not, be changing, and that Tales Across Time will not get any lower in the future.[/b]

So get 'em while they're hot! ;) 

And remember, [b]every purchase goes towards 8-Bit Adventures 2's development.[/b] I don't like to push this too much, but I am funding development myself, [b]so any and all support is greatly appreciated![/b]

[h1][b][u]8-Bit Adventures 2 Battle Animation Preview[/u][/b][/h1]

In my last post about the battle system, all of the pictures I showed were fairly static. So this time I wanted to show off a handful of different battle animations from 8-Bit Adventures 2! They really add a flair to combat and make battles feel a lot more dynamic.

However, please note - Steam's image upload system seems to have sped up the animations a bit. So I apologise if they look a tad too fast. But without further adieu, here are a few of my early favourites: 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/448512149327be155c3844e28e6d7c2a724fc6cb.gif[/img]

Let's start off with an RPG staple - the Fenix Down item! Not only does it butcher the English language, it also revives one fallen party member. I love it when these animations reference the actual namesake (a Phoenix), so I think Jerram (the artist) did a fantastic job!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/203b189909045d229f3a4e0133d845b42cecedef.gif[/img]

Here we have an enemy ability called Identify Weak Point. The Steam-Powered Sentry scans its opponent and (surprise, surprise) identifies their weak points, reducing Physical and Magical Defence.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/1de6bfa39b6ef4251954055b708fe7424fc9bdf7.gif[/img]

This is Warrior's Rend ability - a classic from the first game. Warrior slices through the screen, rending all enemies' Physical Defence in twain (that's 'in half' if you're not being pretentious =P)!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/6c0f64943cefe4d95bd8b0524fdd2ffef60bedb0.gif[/img]

Charlie's Lucky Hit ability is a guaranteed Critical Hit...if it actually hits the enemy. Luckily (see what I did there?), this time it did! This is one the more cartoon-ish animations, but I really love how it turned out =)

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/c47e3edf345d81f8fdc2a50519ff7c3381ffccf8.gif[/img]

The Clockwork Controller boss is able to summon allies to the battlefield with its Command Directive ability. I decided to cut this GIF short before the other enemies spawned, as when they do, there is a white screen flash. It's fine in-game, however as a looping GIF (that's further sped up by Steam), I was concerned it might make some people uncomfortable. So, uh...here's a sneak peek =P

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/e32ee640b105a4f5e3c64f40cf4cce55bc955d36.gif[/img]

And finally we have the Robot's Rocket Punch ability, giving the Overweight Snake enemy a good wallop! The Robot is a very unique party member, because all of its abilities are equipped rather than learnt. It only has access to 3 abilities at any one time, but has no AP/MP, so it can use its abilities freely. This makes the Robot a pretty handy party member if used well!

[h1][b][u]That's All Folks![/u][/b][/h1]

That’s all for now, but please stay tuned for more updates in the (relatively) near future! I always post [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [/b][url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url][b] on Twitter, as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news![/b]

You can also check out the [url=http://www.criticalgames.com.au/8-bit-adventures-2.html]Critical Games Website[/url] for more [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] info and screenshots (including some animated GIFs), or check Facebook at: https://www.facebook.com/CriticalGamesDev

Thank you very much for looking and I hope you enjoyed the preview!

'Till next time!~
Josh

notes.title: Summer Sale + 8-Bit Adventures 2 Battle System Update!
notes.content:
Well, now that E3’s over, it’s time for the Steam Summer Sale! And not only are [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] and [i]Tales Across Time[/i] on sale, but, as promised, I’m also providing a big update on [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] with a deep dive into the game’s battle system!

[h1][b][u]Summer Sale Discounts[/u][/b][/h1]

But first things first - you can now get [b][i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] at 60% off![/b] That means you can own it for just [b]$4 USD![/b] You can also get the [b]fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD)[/b], or the [b]Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)![/b]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/370300

Additionally, my most recent game [b][i]Tales Across Time[/i] is also participating in the sale[/b], making an already cheap game even [b]cheaper![/b] At just [b]$2.69 USD[/b], you really can't beat that price; trust me - I set the prices ;)

http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710

As I said last month, [b]the discounts won't get any lower[/b] and the Wishlist numbers just keep going up (over 3500 for 8-Bit Adventures and over 3000 for Tales Across Time!). 

[b]Every sale contributes to the development of 8-Bit Adventures 2[/b], and I cannot stress enough how much that helps! So if you've been interested in starting a new adventure, or know a friend who would like the games, then this is the perfect time to jump in and support a new project!

But with that out of the way, [b]let’s get onto [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i]![/b]

[h1][b][u]So…how about a release date?[/u][/b][/h1]

For a game that’s coming out in 2017, it probably seems a bit strange that I still haven’t announced a release date. The reason is that I don’t want to commit to a date that I ultimately can’t meet. Delays are always disappointing, and we see them very regularly in this industry.

The game is progressing rapidly, and I am confident that it will be ready this year. But because [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] is developed by such a small team (one person does art, one person does music, one person programmed the battle system, and I do design/writing/gameplay/whatever else), everything takes a long time to get done. 

However, on the flip-side, being so small (and digital only), there aren’t the issues that big publishers run into. We could technically finish the game and release it the next day (although I wouldn’t recommend doing that)! So please don’t be concerned about the lack of a release date. If nothing else, it'll definitely be out before [i]Kingdom Hearts III[/i] ;)

[h1][b][u]The Battle System[/u][/b][/h1]

Okay, onto the main event! Let’s talk about the battle system. As you can see, it’s had quite the visual upgrade (I think Jerram has done a phenomenal job on the backgrounds, monsters, and UI), but there are numerous changes beyond the new coat of paint.

In the interest of transparency, please note that the in-game battles still have some graphical glitches that need to be sorted out. As such, I’ve taken pictures of the gameplay and edited out those issues. Despite the touch-up, the images below are an accurate representation of the battle system as it appears in-game (although small details are always subject to change).

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/6baf29594c0ad18ab9d4bf8db145723327284f6a.gif[/img]

[b]User Interface[/b]

When I first started designing the battle system, I knew that I wanted to have more abilities and commands at the player’s disposal. Where I ran into difficulty was establishing how to fit all of those commands into the UI without making things seem cluttered or unintuitive. The [i]8-Bit Adventures 1[/i] menu system had to go! Eventually, I decided on using icons instead, and ultimately the UI took its inspiration from [i]Mother 3[/i] – in a couple of ways. 

Commands are issued by selecting icons in the top-left corner of the screen. It’s a simple, intuitive way for the player to select the actions they want to take. The other element inspired by [i]Mother 3[/i] is that you can see your characters sticking out from behind their respective status windows. The character that is standing up the highest indicates whose turn it currently is (in the case of the above screenshot, it is Warrior’s turn). However, unlike [i]Mother 3[/i], these character sprites have various poses to accompany each of their actions, which make battles look more dynamic. 

[b]Party Members and the Swap Command[/b]

Now, obviously there’s a lot to talk about here, so let’s start with the basics. The battle system was inspired by [i]Final Fantasy X’s[/i] take on turn-based combat. There are 7 party members in total (3 returning, 4 brand new! More on them in the future), but only 3 can participate in battle at once. However, at any time, your characters can swap in and out of battle. So you *can* technically use all 7 playable characters in a single encounter, and this leads to a lot of new potential strategies.

[b]Personal Skills and Personal Abilities[/b]

Particularly since characters now have several unique factors to take into account, beyond their stats. Not only does each character possess a plethora of special abilities/magic, but also two new mechanics – Personal Skills and Personal Abilities. 

A Personal Skill is a special command unique to a particular character (it’s the second icon on the row), which allows them to perform a special action with no MP/AP cost. For example, Warrior’s Personal Skill is Shield Bash, which allows him to attempt to inflict the ‘Stun’ status on an enemy. If the Stun is successful, he then follows up with an attack. If it’s unsuccessful, though, then no damage is dealt and the turn is wasted. So it’s very much a risk/reward ability. 

A Personal Ability is a passive ability, again unique to a specific character. For example, Warrior has a chance of counterattacking an enemy strike, while Thief gets a speed boost at the start of battle, often allowing her to get the first turn. They’re small additions which make every member of your party feel more distinct, and can feed into interesting strategies. For example, you could include Thief in your party so that she gets the first turn, and then immediately swap her out to allow a different character (perhaps a slower, heavy hitter) to take advantage of that speed boost. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/5d335c6ef32447708ce99df88e8468cda8f2e311.png[/img]

[b]Turn Order System[/b]

On that note, I should explain the new turn system. This is the main element inspired by [i]Final Fantasy X[/i], as each character and enemy now has their own separate turn. In [i]8-Bit Adventures 1[/i], you would select commands for all of your characters and then watch everything play out, but you had no exact way of knowing who would act when.  

Well, now you do! In [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i], you issue commands to each character separately, and the list on the right side of the screen shows you the turn order – i.e. the sequence in which characters and enemies will act. So in the image above, it is currently Thief’s turn. After she’s done, the Clockwork Soldier enemy will have its turn, followed by Warrior, then Mage, then Thief, etc. This also contributes to a deeper level of strategic gameplay, as you can more effectively plan ahead. 

[b]Omega Burst[/b]

In addition to Personal Skills and Abilities, [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] also features a “Limit Break” mechanic titled Omega Burst. Now, if you’re an RPG veteran, you generally know what this entails – each character has a special, ultimate ability which can be used once a bar fills up. The bar is filled up by the player both dishing out and receiving damage. However, Omega Bursts have one unique difference. Rather than each character having their own unique energy bar to fill up, there is a single bar for the entire party. Once it is filled up, every character has the option to use their Omega Burst; but once a character uses it, the bar is completely emptied. 

I decided to take this approach due to my past experience with other RPGs that implement this mechanic. Sometimes in a game like [i]Final Fantasy VII[/i], the character who’s Limit Break I’d want to use wouldn’t get their bar filled in time, while the other two members of my party would. This new ‘one bar fits all’ approach means that you can choose whose Omega Burst to use and when. And since every character contributes to it, the bar fills up a bit quicker than it would in some other RPGs, meaning that you’ll still get to utilise plenty of these attacks in tough battles. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/fa61388f6e907bbac7d2e3239bf717c03fe1b648.png[/img]

[b]Augmentations[/b]

Finally, let’s discuss Augmentations. These are special, passive abilities that are able to be equipped to a character – much like Weapons and Armour. Augmentations can be found in treasure chests, like any other piece of equipment, and provide numerous effects that allow you to further customise your characters. This includes things like increasing a particular stat (e.g. HP+10%), granting immunity to certain status ailments, decreasing the amount of AP/MP it costs to use special abilities/magic, imbuing your ordinary attacks with the ability to inflict negative statuses, and much more. 

Each character has 5 Augmentation slots to use (although you only start off with one open slot – more are unlocked as you progress through the game). Additionally, there is a sixth ‘Special’ slot that only fits character-exclusive augmentations. There are two exclusive augmentations for each character, so you’ll have to decide which of them to equip!

[b]Wrapping Up[/b]

Oh, and one last thing I should mention – the Colour Element system from the first game is no longer a mechanic in [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i]. I was considering it early on, but to put it simply, I feel like I did everything I could with it the first time around. So no more matching colours, but I think the new systems will have plenty of depth =)

And after all that, we still haven’t talked about things like the tiered-attack system, or one particular character’s unique command and equipment system. But I hope this helps convey that [i]8-Bit Adventures 2’s[/i] combat is going to feature a lot of depth and possibilities for interesting strategies. 

With that said, though, if you’re concerned about the mechanics becoming too complicated this time around, please don’t worry. While there are a lot of systems, most of them are pretty simple in practice and you can choose not to engage with them. But if you’re an RPG veteran like myself, then you’ll likely have a lot of fun trying to form your own strategies and customise the party. 

[h1][b][u]Till Next Time![/u][/b][/h1]

That’s all for now, but there will be plenty of news in the (relatively) near future! I always post [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [/b][url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url][b] on Twitter, as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news![/b]

You can also check out the [url=http://www.criticalgames.com.au/8-bit-adventures-2.html]Critical Games Website[/url] for more [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] info and screenshots (including some animated GIFs), or check Facebook at: https://www.facebook.com/CriticalGamesDev

Just an aside, if you’ve been following these posts, you may remember that last year I said that [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] would be renamed at some point. However, I’m currently thinking of keeping the name as 8-Bit Adventures 2. It’s short, simple, and straightforward– at least, compared to 8-Bit Adventures: The Forgotten Journey Remastered Edition =P If nothing else, 8-Bit Adventures 2: Adventure Harder and 8-Bit Adventures 2: 8-Bit Boogaloo are definitely out!

Thank you very much for reading, and I hope everyone has a fantastic Summer (or Winter if you’re in the Southern Hemisphere, like myself)! =D

notes.title: Weeklong Sale Discounts + Enemies of 8-Bit Adventures 2 Sneak Peek!
notes.content:
Hi there! I hope you've all played some great games and been having a fantastic 2017 so far =D If you're looking for something to tide you over until the release of Horizon, Mass Effect, or (my next obsession) Zelda next month, [b]I'm very happy to announce a brand new Weeklong Sale discount![/b] 

In future, I always post future updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter[/b], as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news!

[h1]Weeklong Sale Discounts[/h1]

From 10AM US Pacific Time, you can get [b][i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] at 60% off! [/b]That means you can own it for [b]just $4 USD![/b] You can also get the [b]fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD)[/b], or the [b]Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)![/b]

Additionally, my most recent game [b][i]Tales Across Time[/i] is also participating in the sale,[/b] making an already cheap game even [b]cheaper![/b] At just [b]$2.69 USD[/b], you really can't beat that price; trust me - I set the prices ;)

http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710

[b]The discounts won't get any lower[/b] and the Wishlist numbers just keep going up (3500 for 8-Bit Adventures and over 2800 for Tales Across Time!). So if you've been interested in starting a new adventure, or know a friend who would like the game, then this is the perfect time to jump in. Why, you ask? Well, read on!

[h1]Enemies of 8-Bit Adventures 2 Sneak Peak[/h1]

As many of you know, [b][i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] is coming this year![/b] It is by far the biggest project I've ever developed; Jerram Fahey (the pixel artist), Carfonu (the composer), and myself are all hard at work on it. And if you haven't seen the recent teaser trailer, please check it out here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lg872qrw8Bk
I'm not planning on revealing much about the game until close to release, however I wanted to give you an example of Jerram's recent handiwork - [b]the enemies of 8-Bit Adventures 2![/b] As with all elements of the presentation, the monster graphics have been [b]dramatically[/b] improved for the sequel. 

[b]For example, here's both the Headless Ghost and Overweight Snake[/b] - first as they appeared in 8-Bit Adventures 1, and then their new designs in 8-Bit Adventures 2. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/4a9026cc58e5af134d18b03ef64778bbeaf2f101.png[/img] [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/ee7c03e2dfeac5669538c1cb3cbe6e6458415d7d.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/806c0ba2d85a2b6ed5b12cb1083e2a9dd22807ff.png[/img]            [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/39c926e4653886292889fc4822be690666efda28.png[/img]

As you can see, it's like night and day! But I should note, [b]there are only 4 returning enemies from the first game[/b] - the rest are brand new. There's a lot I can't show due to spoilers, but I wanted to introduce you to a few new enemies. 

[b]First up is Self-Obsessed Squid.[/b] This is an enemy who has two hobbies - going to the Gym and staring at itself the mirror. Some people call it self-obsessed, but it doesn't care - just look at those abs! 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/14d635b4cbd1d8491f3e8417e91ec601e2bc0dc6.png[/img]

[b]Next we have the Rattling Ravager[/b] - a fearsome foe reanimated from animal bones. It makes an unpleasant rattling sound whenever it's about to launch an attack. This is actually the first enemy you encounter in the game!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/910acf4f1b4ccef0c9702f8c779e492a7b64cafa.png[/img]

[b]CRUSH!! is a big rock.[/b] He likes to crush things. Particularly player characters. If CRUSH!! had to describe himself, CRUSH!! might say that he’s the illegitimate love child of a Thwomp from Mario and a Rockbomb from Dragon Quest. But that's assuming CRUSH!! could talk...which he can't. Makes you wonder why he has a mouth, really. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/45e4871f945f56b086beb8c10de199c00cd8362a.png[/img]

[b]And last but not least, we have the Clockwork Controller[/b] - a boss enemy. Without giving much away, let's just say that this foe comes from a very different place than the rest of these enemies. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/7ea55535dce20691e38fe3779245e5b5d4fda470.png[/img]

[h1]'Till Next Time![/h1]

I hope that everyone enjoyed this quick look at the enemies of [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] - [b]there's plenty more to come throughout the year![/b] 

And as always, I’ll post future updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter[/b], as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news!

I sincerely appreciate your continued patience and support, and as always [b]I hope that this Weeklong Sale allows even more players to enjoy [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] and [i]Tales Across Time[/i]![/b]

In future, I always post future updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter[/b], as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news!

[h1]Weeklong Sale Discounts[/h1]

From 10AM US Pacific Time, you can get [b][i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] at 60% off! [/b]That means you can own it for [b]just $4 USD![/b] You can also get the [b]fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 30% off ($3.50 USD)[/b], or the [b]Game + Soundtrack bundle 45% off (that’s only $6.60 USD)![/b]

Additionally, my most recent game [b][i]Tales Across Time[/i] is also participating in the sale,[/b] making an already cheap game even [b]cheaper![/b] At just [b]$2.69 USD[/b], you really can't beat that price; trust me - I set the prices ;)

http://store.steampowered.com/app/461710

[b]The discounts won't get any lower[/b] and the Wishlist numbers just keep going up (3500 for 8-Bit Adventures and over 2800 for Tales Across Time!). So if you've been interested in starting a new adventure, or know a friend who would like the game, then this is the perfect time to jump in. Why, you ask? Well, read on!

[h1]Enemies of 8-Bit Adventures 2 Sneak Peak[/h1]

As many of you know, [b][i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] is coming this year![/b] It is by far the biggest project I've ever developed; Jerram Fahey (the pixel artist), Carfonu (the composer), and myself are all hard at work on it. And if you haven't seen the recent teaser trailer, please check it out here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lg872qrw8Bk
I'm not planning on revealing much about the game until close to release, however I wanted to give you an example of Jerram's recent handiwork - [b]the enemies of 8-Bit Adventures 2![/b] As with all elements of the presentation, the monster graphics have been [b]dramatically[/b] improved for the sequel. 

[b]For example, here's both the Headless Ghost and Overweight Snake[/b] - first as they appeared in 8-Bit Adventures 1, and then their new designs in 8-Bit Adventures 2. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/4a9026cc58e5af134d18b03ef64778bbeaf2f101.png[/img] [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/ee7c03e2dfeac5669538c1cb3cbe6e6458415d7d.png[/img]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/806c0ba2d85a2b6ed5b12cb1083e2a9dd22807ff.png[/img]            [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/39c926e4653886292889fc4822be690666efda28.png[/img]

As you can see, it's like night and day! But I should note, [b]there are only 4 returning enemies from the first game[/b] - the rest are brand new. There's a lot I can't show due to spoilers, but I wanted to introduce you to a few new enemies. 

[b]First up is Self-Obsessed Squid.[/b] This is an enemy who has two hobbies - going to the Gym and staring at itself the mirror. Some people call it self-obsessed, but it doesn't care - just look at those abs! 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/14d635b4cbd1d8491f3e8417e91ec601e2bc0dc6.png[/img]

[b]Next we have the Rattling Ravager[/b] - a fearsome foe reanimated from animal bones. It makes an unpleasant rattling sound whenever it's about to launch an attack. This is actually the first enemy you encounter in the game!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/910acf4f1b4ccef0c9702f8c779e492a7b64cafa.png[/img]

[b]CRUSH!! is a big rock.[/b] He likes to crush things. Particularly player characters. If CRUSH!! had to describe himself, CRUSH!! might say that he’s the illegitimate love child of a Thwomp from Mario and a Rockbomb from Dragon Quest. But that's assuming CRUSH!! could talk...which he can't. Makes you wonder why he has a mouth, really. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/45e4871f945f56b086beb8c10de199c00cd8362a.png[/img]

[b]And last but not least, we have the Clockwork Controller[/b] - a boss enemy. Without giving much away, let's just say that this foe comes from a very different place than the rest of these enemies. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8798587/7ea55535dce20691e38fe3779245e5b5d4fda470.png[/img]

[h1]'Till Next Time![/h1]

I hope that everyone enjoyed this quick look at the enemies of [i]8-Bit Adventures 2[/i] - [b]there's plenty more to come throughout the year![/b] 

And as always, I’ll post future updates here on Steam, but [b]I also highly recommend following [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU[/url] on Twitter[/b], as that’s the best way I’ve found to keep up-to-date on news!

I sincerely appreciate your continued patience and support, and as always [b]I hope that this Weeklong Sale allows even more players to enjoy [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] and [i]Tales Across Time[/i]![/b]

notes.title: NEW GAME - Tales Across Time - on Steam Greenlight!
notes.content:
As anyone who's followed me on Twitter knows, it's taken a bit longer than expected, but I am very excited to announce that my newest game - [i]Tales Across Time[/i] - is now on Steam Greenlight! 

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=630959133
This is the first step in getting the game released on Steam, but I can't do it without your help! If you'd like to support my work (including the development of '8-Bit Adventures 2'), please check out the page and give [i]Tales Across Time[/i] a 'Yes' vote.  I would sincerely appreciate it =)

There might also be a little something for [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] fans on that page too ;)

[i]Tales Across Time[/i] is a narrative-driven RPG which uses the short-story format to tell the tale of three very different characters; each living centuries apart, but in the same location. 

[b]It Features:[/b]
[list]
[*][i]Experience Three Gripping Tales[/i], each set in a different time period.
[*][i]Unique Turn-Based Battle System[/i] - built around resource management & one-on-one encounters. 
[*][i]Discover Engaging Characters[/i] and People with Personality. 
[*][i]Same Location, Different Environment[/i] - explore a familiar land, transformed by the passage of time. 
[*][i]Battle a Wide Variety of Monsters[/i], which constantly change-up combat.
[*][i]A Narrative-Focused Experience[/i] - keeps the story going and doesn’t waste your time (no grinding/filler). 
[/list]

Thank you very much for your support everyone! =D

notes.title: Holiday Sale, Thank You, & Future Projects!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

[h1][b]Holiday Sale[/b][/h1]

I’m happy to announce that [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] is 50% off in this year’s Steam Holiday Sale – that means you can own it for just $5 USD! And that’s not all. You can also get the fantastic Remastered Soundtrack 20% off ($4 USD), or the Game + Soundtrack bundle 34% off (that’s only $7.91 USD)!

I know that well over 1000 people still have the game and soundtrack on their wishlist, so now’s a great time to start your own 8-Bit Adventure! =)

As always, I like to spotlight recent player reviews. I make sure to read every single one (including those in other languages), and sincerely appreciate all of the wonderful feedback:

[quote=VodkaFun]
[b]8-Bit Adventures wow what a game. Had this title been released somewhere been 1985 and 1989 it would of been right up on that pedestal with the great RPGS of that time. Just playing through this game you can see the amount of time and love the dev has put into it.[/b][/quote]
[quote=TheJerodian]
[b]Can't say enough about this game. Especially since there is a lot that has already been said…If you like RPGs and Steam achievements, getting this game is a win-win!

...Lastly the music is very enjoyable! If you like FF1 type 8-bit music, then I'd recommend getting the soundtrack as well![/b][/quote]
[quote=Welly welly welly well]
[b]Definitely one of my favorite games ever.

I got this game in a bundle and I left it in my library for far too long just because I didn't have any great expectations for this game. Boy, was I wrong...This brilliant game made me laugh, cry, and ship characters. It's amazing how every NPC is interesting. 

Anyway, I'm so glad that I finally got to play this masterpiece. I wish more people knew about this game. It deserves more love.[/b][/quote]

[h1][b]Thank You![/b][/h1]

On a slightly more personal note, I wanted to thank each and every person who’s purchased [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i], reviewed it on Steam, or posted on the forums. 2015 has been my best year in a long time, and you guys have given me the confidence to move forward with other projects. It was only 8 short months ago that I was preparing to give up on my dream and leave game development behind. So from the bottom of my heart, thank you all for being awesome =D

[h1][b]Future Projects[/b][/h1]

But enough of that - let’s talk about the future. In 2016, I’m planning to release two games. The first is called [i]Tales Across Time[/i] and will be launching very early next year. It’s an RPG featuring a unique turn-based battle system, and is a much more linear and story-focused experience than something like [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i]. Please stay tuned for more information coming soon!

And I’m very happy to officially announce that "8-Bit Adventures 2" is in development and will be released in 2016. It’s still very early days, but I can say that I’m working with a new engine (RPG Maker MV) which will result in a much smoother experience for players (and no more resolution issues!). Almost all of the money I’ve earned from [i]8-Bit Adventures Remastered Edition[/i] is going into this project, so you can expect a much-improved visual experience. 

To give you a taste of this, I re-created a map from the original [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i]. Keep in mind that everything is work-in-progress, and the character sprites are recycled from the first game, but I hope this gives you some idea of what to expect. You can take a look [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU/status/679403528222195719]here.[/url] Please note, the second image is taken directly from the original game, and is included for comparison.

If you want to keep up with future announcements, please make sure to check the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/8bitadventures/announcements/]8-Bit Adventures Steam Community[/url] or follow [url=https://twitter.com/CriticalGamesAU]@CriticalGamesAU on Twitter.[/url]

I hope everyone has a very Merry Christmas and/or Happy Holidays, and a wonderful New Year. See you in 2016! =D

notes.title: New FREE Game! 8-Bit Adventures Update 2.1! Soundtrack Bundle Released!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! It's been about a month since my last post, so there's plenty of news to report. 

[h1]First up is a new game - [i]Tales Across Time[/i]![/h1] I developed this title for the 2015 Indie Game Maker Contest, which means it's 100% free to play! I'd say if you liked [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i], you'll probably enjoy this game too. It can be found here:

http://contest.gamedevfort.com/submission/721#.Vcf5wvnaQTY

[i]Tales Across Time[/i] is comprised of three 'short-stories', told using traditional RPG mechanics. Each tale takes place in the same location, but separated by hundreds of years. In this 1 hour+ adventure, you will explore ancient ruins, help a woman save her fiancée, and be hunted by a masked man!

The contest required developers to create a game within a month, which is a very short amount of time to make an RPG, so please keep that in mind. But if you do enjoy the game, I would sincerely appreciate a vote (just hit that little blue 'Vote +1' button). There are numerous prizes, including the People's Choice award, so your votes are a massive help!

Okay, I think that's enough self-promotion =) 

[h1]In other news, Update 2.1 for 8-Bit Adventures has been released![/h1] This new version fixes two very nasty bugs.[list]
[*]You can no longer be locked out of the Sky Forge. The Gemstone still disappears, but now the door remains open.
[*]You can no longer skip a very important cutscene in the Turcosa Swamp. In previous versions, there was a spot which allowed you to walk around the triggers and skip this sequence - which could result in a dead game.
[/list]
I sincerely apologise to anyone that has encountered these issues, and a big thanks to everyone who reported them. They should now be a thing of the past!

[h1]Finally, I wanted to highlight the release of the Soundtrack Bundle![/h1] Now you can get [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i] together with the Remastered Soundtrack for a reduced price! You can find the bundle on the main Store page here:

http://store.steampowered.com/app/370300
Or alternatively, you can buy the Remastered Soundtrack (which also comes with the complete, original 8-Bit Soundtrack) separately here:

http://store.steampowered.com/app/387170/?snr=1_5_1100__1100
Regardless, it's a fantastic release that Carfonu (the composer of [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i]) worked very hard on. [b]If you enjoyed the music of [i]8-Bit Adventures[/i], and love orchestral remixes, I cannot recommend it enough![/b]

Phew! That was a lot to get through. As always, a massive thanks to everyone who's been posting on the forum and writing reviews - I honestly can't tell you how much I appreciate all of your comments =)

So thank you very much for your time, and I hope that everyone enjoys these new releases!

notes.title: Update 2.0 (Steam Achievements) Now Available!
notes.content:
I am very happy to announce that Update 2.0 has just been released on Steam! This contains several bug fixes and a brand new addition to the game - Steam Achievements! There's a total of 40 to unlock. Several players have requested this, so I hope that all the Achievement hunters out there enjoy it!

I have posted another topic which details every Achievement that is permanently missable, so if you're worried about skipping something important, please check it out: http://steamcommunity.com/app/370300/discussions/0/618463738380868530/

[h1]Update 2.0[/h1]
[list]
[*]Steam Achievements are now available to unlock! There are 40 achievements in total, which feature a variety of goals.
[*]A small change to the Status Screen. It now displays your Maximum HP and MP, instead of your current HP and MP.
[*]Fixed a typo in the 3rd Dungeon involving a Treasure Chest.
[*]Fixed a bug which allowed the player to get an unused beta item (the Filled Bottle) from the spring in the 2nd Dungeon.
[*]Fixed a typo in a cutscene before fighting the boss of the Sky Forge.
[*]You can no longer land on deep water with the Airship. In previous versions, the player could get stuck doing this.
[*]A small change to the Escape Amulet in the final dungeon which fixes a potential graphical glitch.
[*]Fixed a small graphical glitch in the ending sequence.
[*]You can no longer get two pieces of Ultimate Equipment from the same treasure chest at the top of the Overgrown Temple. This was a bug and has been fixed.
[/list]

These changes and additions were all made due to forum posts in the Steam Community, so thank you all very much for writing! I hope every player enjoys these improvements =D

[list]
[*]Steam Achievements are now available to unlock! There are 40 achievements in total, which feature a variety of goals.
[*]A small change to the Status Screen. It now displays your Maximum HP and MP, instead of your current HP and MP.
[*]Fixed a typo in the 3rd Dungeon involving a Treasure Chest.
[*]Fixed a bug which allowed the player to get an unused beta item (the Filled Bottle) from the spring in the 2nd Dungeon.
[*]Fixed a typo in a cutscene before fighting the boss of the Sky Forge.
[*]You can no longer land on deep water with the Airship. In previous versions, the player could get stuck doing this.
[*]A small change to the Escape Amulet in the final dungeon which fixes a potential graphical glitch.
[*]Fixed a small graphical glitch in the ending sequence.
[*]You can no longer get two pieces of Ultimate Equipment from the same treasure chest at the top of the Overgrown Temple. This was a bug and has been fixed.
[/list]

These changes and additions were all made due to forum posts in the Steam Community, so thank you all very much for writing! I hope every player enjoys these improvements =D
